Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with

Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$e_i',e_i''$ be the skew derivations of
[[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]].

(i) **One step.** If $x\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ with $\nu\ne0$ satisfies
$e_i'(x)=0$ for all $i\in I$, then $x=0$.

(ii) **Iterated separation.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ there is a
sequence $i_1,\dots,i_k\in I$ with $\nu=\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}$ (the
multiset is uniquely determined by $\nu$, because the simple roots freely
generate $Q$, and $k=\operatorname{ht}(\nu)$) such that
$e_{i_k}'\cdots e_{i_2}'e_{i_1}'(x)\ne0$. Here the composite is read with the
rightmost factor applied first, so the first chosen derivation $e_{i_1}'$ acts
first; equivalently, the common kernel, on $U_q^-[-\nu]$, of all composites
$e_{i_1}'\cdots e_{i_k}'$ over all such sequences is zero.

The same statements hold with $e_i''$ in place of $e_i'$. This separation property is used by the crystal development and the categorification pairing.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. $$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. $$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$

$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$

derivations.claim: **The barred equation.** Bar the intertwining equation with $B=\psi\otimes\psi$: from $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$ and [F2] one gets $\overline\Delta(\psi(u))\,\overline\Theta=\overline\Theta\,\Delta(\psi(u))$ for every $u$, i.e. after replacing $u$ by $\psi(u)$, $\overline\Delta(u)\overline\Theta=\overline\Theta\Delta(u)$. Inverting the original equation in the convolution algebra [F3] gives $\Theta^{-1}\Delta(u)=\overline\Delta(u)\Theta^{-1}$; applying the algebra automorphism $B$ and using [F2] turns this into $\Delta(\psi(u))B(\Theta^{-1})=B(\Theta^{-1})\overline\Delta(\psi(u))$.

**The coproduct factorizations by duality.** Fix degrees $\gamma,\eta$. In the corresponding component of $\Delta x$, $x\in U^+[\gamma+\eta]$, remove the middle torus to write the coefficient tensor as $x_1\otimes K_{-\eta}x_2$, with $|x_1|=\eta$, $|x_2|=\gamma$. The Hopf adjunction for $D$ gives $\sum D(x_1,z)D(x_2,y)=q^{(\eta,\gamma)}D(x,yz)$ for $y\in U^-[-\gamma]$, $z\in U^-[-\eta]$: in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}x$ the toral pairing is $D(K_{-\eta},K_\gamma)=q^{-(\eta,\gamma)}$. Contract the first two root slots of $(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta$ with these two functionals; the result is $q^{(\eta,\gamma)}yz$. The proposed right side has the same contraction, since $x_2K_{-\eta}=q^{(\eta,\gamma)}K_{-\eta}x_2$ and the two coevaluations contract to $y,z$. This proves the first identity by perfectness. For the second, the degree component of $\Delta u$ for $u\in U^-[-\gamma-\eta]$ is $u_1K_\eta\otimes u_2$. The other Hopf adjunction gives $\sum D(a,u_1)D(b,u_2)=D(ab,u)$ for $a\in U^+[\gamma]$, $b\in U^+[\eta]$; the first pairing with $u_1K_\eta$ has no additional scalar, by the counit term of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}a$. Contracting the last two root slots on each proposed side therefore gives $ab$. This proves the second identity. All tests are in finite homogeneous components; the toral directions are retained, not discarded.

**Identification of the inverse.** Put $Y:=B(\Theta^{-1})=\overline{\Theta^{-1}}$. Step 1.1 shows $\Delta(v)Y=Y\overline\Delta(v)$ for every $v$, and $Y_0=B(\Theta_0)=1$; by the uniqueness clause of [F1], $Y=\Theta$, hence $\Theta^{-1}=B(\Theta)=\overline\Theta$. The inverse is taken in the same positive-first/negative-second completion, because the convolution algebra of [F3] is closed under inversion and $B$ is an automorphism of it; no opposite tensor completion is used.

**Rank-one check in every degree.** Put $t_n=[n]_{q_i^2}!=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}[n]_i!$. The Gaussian coproduct expansions are $\Delta(E_i^{(n)})=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=n}q_i^{\gamma\eta}E_i^{(\eta)}\otimes K_i^{-\eta}E_i^{(\gamma)}$ and $\Delta(F_i^{(n)})=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=n}q_i^{-\gamma\eta}F_i^{(\gamma)}K_i^\eta\otimes F_i^{(\eta)}$. Also $\binom n\gamma_i t_\gamma t_\eta=q_i^{-\gamma\eta}t_n$. In (ii)'s first right side, toral crossing $E_i^{(\gamma)}K_i^{-\eta}=q_i^{2\gamma\eta}K_i^{-\eta}E_i^{(\gamma)}$ and divided-power multiplication produce the coefficient $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^nt_nq_i^{\gamma\eta}$. In the second right side, no toral crossing is needed and the coefficient is $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^nt_nq_i^{-\gamma\eta}$. These are precisely the two left-side coproduct coefficients.

**The barred coproduct identity.** Let $r(u)$ be the negative-half twisted coproduct obtained from $\Delta u$ by removing $K$-factors, with tensor multiplication twisted by $q^{-(\beta,\gamma)}$. Its bar counterpart satisfies $\bar r(u)_{\eta,\gamma}=q^{(\eta,\gamma)}\operatorname{flip}(r(u)_{\gamma,\eta})$: both sides send $F_i$ to $F_i\otimes1+1\otimes F_i$, and the scalar twist verifies multiplicativity on homogeneous products. In $\overline\Delta u$, moving the torus to the left contributes $q^{-(\eta,\gamma)}$ and cancels this factor. Thus, after removing the middle torus $K_{-\gamma}$, the $(\eta,\gamma)$ coefficient of $\overline\Delta u$ is the flip of $r(u)_{\gamma,\eta}$. The Hopf multiplication adjunction used in step 1.2 now shows that contraction of the last two root slots of $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta$ gives $ab$, with $a$ testing degree $\gamma$ and $b$ degree $\eta$. The same contraction of $(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}K_{-\gamma}^{(2)}(\Theta_\eta)_{12}$ gives $ab$. Perfectness proves (iv).

**The cocycle identity.** Summing (ii)'s first identity, and noting that the middle torus commutes with every outer $(\Theta_\eta)_{13}$, gives $((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=\Theta_{23}(\sum_\eta(\Theta_\eta)_{13}K_{-\eta}^{(2)})\Theta_{12}$. Applying $\Delta(y)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(y)$ in the last two positions to each second-factor coefficient $y$ of $\Theta$ gives $\Theta_{23}(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23}$. This proves (iii). All operations are coefficientwise in the threefold completion, or finite on the stated admissible vectors. No middle torus is commuted through a $(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}$ term.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

For a balanced triple, the two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If the triple is balanced and $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

Let $\psi$ (the bar involution) and $\tau$ (the contravariant anti-involution) be
the semilinear maps of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so
that $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$
and $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$, $\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$,
with $\tau$ anti-multiplicative. Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$ be
the Lusztig divided-power integral form with its generators $E_i^{(r)}$,
$F_i^{(r)}$, $K_h^{\pm1}$ and toral binomials $T_{i,c,t}$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then $\psi(U_A)=U_A$ and
$\tau(U_A)=U_A$. Explicitly, on the generators,

$$\psi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \psi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t},$$

$$\tau(E_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \tau(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}.$$

In particular both maps restrict to bijections of $U_A$: $\psi$ to a semilinear
algebra involution of $U_A$ and $\tau$ to a semilinear anti-involution of
$U_A$, while $q^{\pm1}\in A$ keeps all coefficients in $A$. These are the two
involutions under which the bar lattice and the contravariant duality of the
later constructions are taken; neither formula is the Chevalley involution
$\omega$, which changes signs, exchanges the two halves and is treated in
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
No choice is used.

Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at $0$ and at infinity, and the integral affine chart coordinate rings are $\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in P^+$. Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$, well defined by the highest-module presentation: its negative-half kernel is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}$, preserved by $\psi$ because every $F_i$ is fixed ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. Hence the quotient involution is compatible with the algebra action and fixes $v_\lambda$. Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]); both are $\psi$-stable. Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$.

The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction on this page, whereas $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice $M_A$. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. The intersections $M_A\cap L$ and $M_A\cap L^-$ are respectively $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-modules, generally not $A$-modules. The balanced part $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module; its Laurent extension $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$ is the full integral module once globalization is proved.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

derivations.claim: **Existence.** Apply [F1] degree by degree, and note that the residue target is the free $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B$ in each finite root or label component. The lift $G(b)$ of residue $b$ exists in $E_{\mathbb Z}$, is bar invariant by [F1], and the direct sums over degrees give a family $G(\mathcal B)$ with the asserted spanning properties over $A$, $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; adaptedness to the string ideals is the corresponding clause of [F1].

**Uniqueness.** Let $g,h\in M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ have the same residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$. Then $g-h\in E_{\mathbb Z}\cap qL$ lies in the kernel of the canonical map of [F2], which is injective in the balanced case; hence $g=h$. Applied to $g=G(b)$ and an arbitrary lift of $b$, this is exactly the uniqueness used by later consumers, and it identifies the family defined over either chart.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 give existence, the residue normalization, bar invariance, the two chart-basis assertions, the balanced-intersection and field-span descriptions and uniqueness; no word family, unitriangular condition or lower self-duality enters, since the construction is the inverse of the integral globalization map of [F2].

Let $i\in I$ and let $e_i'$ be the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with string decomposition $u=\sum_lF_i^{(l)}u_l$, $u_l\in\ker e_i'$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]).

(i) If $u\in U_A^-$ then all $u_l$ lie in $U_A^-$. The integral projector is
$$P_i=\sum_l(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}(e_i')^l,\qquad u_l=q_i^{l(l-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^lu,$$
where all powers of $e_i'$ are ordinary powers, not divided by $[l]_i!$.

(ii) Define
$$I_{(i,n)}^A:=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-=\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}\bigl(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-,$$
$$J_{(i,n)}^A:=\pi_\lambda\bigl(I_{(i,n)}^A\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda),$$
with $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ as in [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]]. The latter is an $A$-submodule inside the field string-image subspace $F_i^nV(\lambda)$, not a $U_q$-submodule or a $U_A$-stable lattice in general; its equality with $V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed here.

(iii) The integral residue of $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is the free $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$, and the corresponding rational residue of $F_i^nU_q^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is its $\mathbb Q$-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple of $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is a conclusion of the subsequent string-ideal induction, not an input.

(iv) On every $U_A$-stable integrable module lattice $M_A$, if a label $\mu$ satisfies $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=-n\le-1$, then every $u\in(M_A)_\mu$ satisfies the finite identity
$$u=\sum_{k\ge n}(-1)^{k-n}\binom{k-1}{k-n}_iF_i^{(k)}E_i^{(k)}u,$$
and consequently $(M_A)_\mu=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k)}(M_A)_{\mu+k\alpha_i}$. This is the exact boundary generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.

(i) the image string ideal $J_{(i,n)}^A$ in each highest module $V(\lambda)$, with its rational zero- and infinity-chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree $\lambda-\alpha$, and its balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection maps isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\lambda\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\lambda$ in that degree;

(ii) the half ideal $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is integrally balanced in degree $-\alpha$, with balanced intersection mapping isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\infty\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\infty$; and

(iii) their Laurent extensions are free $A$-modules with the adapted global lifts.

Let $\star$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear anti-involution of $U_q^-$ fixing each generator $F_i$, so that for a word $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$ one has $(F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r})^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, and let $B$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then $\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution of the Serre quotient, reverses negative words, preserves the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], commutes with the bar involution $\psi$, and preserves $B$: $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$. Consequently $\star$ preserves the crystal lattice $\mathcal L(\infty)$ of [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], the integral residue lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$, and the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-=U_A^-\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ of [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]]. On the integral crystal residue the induced map permutes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. Only this signed lattice preservation is asserted, not an unsigned $\star$-crystal theorem; the sign is what the gluing of the string-ideal global lifts requires.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$. Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(d) **Large-weight form.** If all $\lambda(h_j)$, $j\in I$, are sufficiently large compared with $\alpha$, then $\pi_\lambda$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the congruences of (b) for such $\lambda$ are the computation used inside the grand loop to deduce the general case; the general statements (a)-(c) hold for every $\lambda\in P^+$, without a largeness hypothesis.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: clause (c) is clause N(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof applies clause J(r), and J(r) is where the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] is used. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral, so $m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$
for all $i$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with highest vector
$v_\lambda$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).
Put $s_i:=F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$.

(i) Every $s_i$ is a singular (highest weight) vector of weight
$\lambda-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$.

(ii) The graded submodule
$S:=\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)s_i=\sum_iU_q^-s_i$ is proper, and the quotient
$\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/S$ is nonzero, has finite-dimensional
label-weight spaces, and is integrable ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

(iii) Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of highest weight
$\lambda$ is a quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices
with $a_{ij}\ne0$ is assumed anywhere.

derivations.claim: **The based quotient.** Since $G_\infty(\mathcal B(\infty))$ is an $A$-basis of $U_A^-$ and $\pi_\lambda$ is $A$-linear, the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of the basis elements mapped to $0$, and the surviving basis elements map onto $V_A(\lambda)$; by [F1] the killed elements are exactly those with $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$, the surviving images are exactly the $A$-basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, and the correspondence is bijective on residues. The weight components of $V_A(\lambda)$ are finite free over $A$ because they have the finite basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu)$, and the chart and residue projections are the compatible maps of [F3]. This proves (i).

**The field kernel and its saturated ideals.** By [F4] the field kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_q^-$ is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{s_i}$ with $s_i:=\lambda(h_i)+1$. By [F2] each $U_q^-F_i^{s_i}$ is the field span of the signed global family of the saturated right ideal $R_{(i,s_i)}^A=U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{s_i}$, and the field span of a sum of subspaces is the span of the union of their spanning subsets of the single global basis. Intersecting with the free $A$-lattice $U_A^-$ gives exactly the $A$-span of that union, i.e. $\ker(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-})=\sum_iR_{(i,s_i)}^A$.

**The divided-power form of the kernel.** By [F2] again, $R_{(i,s)}^A=\sum_{t\ge s}U_A^-F_i^{(t)}$ for every $s$, since every element of $U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{s}$ is an integral combination of products $uF_i^{(t)}$ with $t\ge s$ and conversely each $U_A^-F_i^{(t)}\subseteq U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{s}$ for $t\ge s$. Substituting $s=s_i=\lambda(h_i)+1$ into step 1.2 gives $\ker(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-})=\sum_i\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}$, the asserted integral presentation by all divided right powers beyond each highest limit.

**Conclusion.** Step 1.1 proves the based quotient, kernel-description, basis bijection, finiteness and chart compatibility of (i); steps 1.2 and 2.1 prove the exact integral kernel of (ii), using the reversal symmetry between left string ideals and saturated right ideals and avoiding any unproved commutation of integral intersections with sums. The Choice use is confined to [C1].

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] on $U_q^-$, and let $\iota:U_q^+	o U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$ (equivalently, the library's signed Chevalley involution composed with the compensating degree sign, [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]]). For $x\in U_q^+$ of degree $
u\in Q_+$ and $y\in U_q^-$ of degree $-
u$ define
$$D(x,y):=d_
u^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_
u:=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{
u_i},$$
and set $D(x,y):=0$ when the degrees are not opposite. Then $D$ is homogeneous and bilinear, $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$, and
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})= rac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n},$$
by [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]], with $E_i^{(n)}\mapsto F_i^{(n)}$ under $\iota$ and $q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_i!=1/[n]_{q_i^2}!$ for the geometric factorial of that item. The pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$ ([[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]); it is not this quasi-$R$/Drinfeld normalization. The completed normalized tensor of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]] uses the $D$-dual bases.

On the simple-root Borel extensions the toral normalization is $D(K_
u,K_\mu)=q^{(
u,\mu)}$ for $
u,\mu\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}I$ (the embedded simple-root toral directions), with mixed toral/root generator pairings $0$ and counit normalization $D(1,1)=1$; the Hopf adjunction identities use $\Delta$ on the negative Borel and $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ on the positive Borel ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]). No pairing on arbitrary extra toral directions of $P^\vee$ is asserted. The divided-power integral form constrained here is that of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]; no integrality of $D$ is claimed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), put
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), let
$L:=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb Z(d_ih_i)\subseteq P^{\vee}$, and let $U_A^0$ be the
$A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the toral quantum
binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]).

(a) **One simple torus.** Fix $i\in I$ and write $z:=q_i$, $K:=K_i$,
$T_t:=T_{i,0,t}$ for $t\ge0$. Then for all $r,s\ge0$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and
$t\ge1$,
$$T_rT_s=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(r,s)}z^{rs}K^{-j}\binom{r+s-j}{r}_z\binom{r}{j}_zT_{r+s-j},\qquad T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^{-1}z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1},$$
where $\binom{m}{r}_z$ is the Gaussian binomial of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]; all
coefficients lie in $A$. Moreover the $A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by
$K^{\pm1}$ and all $T_{c,t}$ equals the $A$-span of
$\{K^{\delta}T_t:\delta\in\{0,1\},\,t\ge0\}$, and that set is an $A$-basis.

(b) **Full torus.** Fix a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $P^{\vee}$, let $J$ be the
finite set of coordinates occurring in the finitely many vectors $d_ih_i$, and
let $D:=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathbb Z e_j$ be the corresponding coordinate direct
summand. For every coset of $L$ in $P^{\vee}$ choose the representative $c$
whose $D$-component has minimal sum of coordinate absolute values, ties broken
lexicographically, and whose complementary component is the coset's common
complementary component. Then
$$U_A^0=\bigoplus_{c}K_c\cdot A\text{-span}\Bigl\{\prod_{i\in I}K_i^{\delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}:\delta_i\in\{0,1\},\,t_i\ge0\Bigr\},$$
the sum over the chosen representatives, so the displayed elements form an
$A$-basis of $U_A^0$.

Both statements are proved directly on the unmodified generators over the
non-PID ring $A$: no integral PBW or canonical-basis input, no inference from
torsion-freeness to freeness, and no modified-${}_A\dot U$ result is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, $K=\mathbb C((\hbar))$, $q=e^\hbar$, and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$ for a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum. Let $H^+=U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$ and the shuffle product be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], and put $H^-=T(V^*)/J_-$ using [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]. Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the formal embedding theorem. For an indeterminate $z$, let $H_z^\pm$ be the algebras over $\mathbb C(z)$ presented by the separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, with parameters $z_i=z^{d_i}$.

(i) Each $H^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is finite free over $R$, and
$$\operatorname{rank}_R H^\pm[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^\pm)[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(z)}H_z^\pm[\pm\alpha].$$
Every family of homogeneous lifts of a basis of the classical component is an $R$-basis. Likewise, homogeneous word expressions with coefficients rational in $z$, regular at $z=1$, which reduce to a classical component basis form a basis of the corresponding generic component. In particular, for a supplied ordered homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak n^\pm$, ordered monomials in any such regular lifts form a generic PBW basis.

(ii) Both formal halves are graded braided Hopf algebras. Their generators are primitive, their counits kill positive height, and their tensor squares use
$$ (u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv',\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij},$$
with negative degrees for $H^-$. The word pairing restricts and descends to a nondegenerate $K$-valued pairing $H^+\times H^-$ with $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/(\hbar d_i)$ and $\langle1,1\rangle=1$. It is zero on unequal opposite degrees and satisfies the braided Hopf adjunctions
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad\langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle.$$
The generic halves have the same braided Hopf structures and a nondegenerate $\mathbb C(z)$-valued pairing normalized by $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle_z=\delta_{ij}/(z_i-z_i^{-1})$. Thus opposite graded components are dual. All generic assertions also hold for the corresponding $\mathbb Q(z)$-presentations and their rational pairing, with the PBW lift clause using bases of the rational classical Serre form.

derivations.claim: **Freeness of the factors.** By [F2] the negative half is a direct sum of free $A$-modules $U_A^-[-\gamma]$ of finite rank; by the transport $\iota$ the same holds for $U_A^+$; and by [F3] the unmodified torus $U_A^0$ has the displayed $A$-basis. Each factor is therefore a free $A$-module, and the half factors have finite free root components; the toral degree-zero component can have infinite rank.

**Surjectivity of the multiplication map.** The spanning statement of [F1] says that every element of $U_A$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of products $b_-ub_+$; grouping the factors according to root degree exhibits $U_A$ as the image of $U_A^-\otimes_AU_A^0\otimes_AU_A^+\to U_A$, so the map is surjective.

**Injectivity by field decomposition and torsion-freeness.** Extending scalars along $A\hookrightarrow\mathbb Q(q)$ gives the field multiplication map, which is an isomorphism by [F4]. If $x$ lay in the kernel of the integral map, its image in $U_q^-\otimes U_q^0\otimes U_q^+$ would lie in the kernel of the field isomorphism after extension and hence would be $0$; but the source is a free, hence torsion-free, $A$-module, so the natural map from it to its $\mathbb Q(q)$-extension is injective, forcing $x=0$. Thus the multiplication map is an isomorphism, proving (i).

**Toral basis, freeness and the homogeneous form.** Statement (iii) is the combination of the toral basis [F3] with the factorization of step 2.1; since a tensor product of free modules is free, $U_A$ is free, and restricting the isomorphism to homogeneous components gives the displayed degree-$\beta$ decomposition, with $U_A^0$ contributing only degree $0$. Unique coefficients are those of the products of the chosen basis elements of the three factors, not of arbitrary sums of simple tensors, because the isomorphism is one of $A$-modules with the displayed direct-sum decomposition.

**Ranks and conclusion.** The ranks of the half components are their field dimensions by [F2]; by [F5], applied with its stated Choice hypothesis [C1], those dimensions equal the classical PBW ranks, proving (ii). Steps 1.1–3.1 prove (i), (iii) and (iv); no torsionfree-to-free conversion over the non-PID ring $A$ and no modified dot-$U$ basis was used, since freeness came from explicit bases.

citations.quote: For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$,
$U_A$ the integral form of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], and $k$
a characteristic-zero field regarded as an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$. Let
$\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}}$ be the classical Lie algebra presented by
generators $e_i,f_i,h_i$ with the Cartan and Serre relations, its Cartan being
the span of the independent simple coroots
([[thm-serre-presentation-of-a-kac-moody-algebra]]).

(a) **Halves.** $U_A^\pm\otimes_Ak\cong U(\mathfrak n^\pm)_k$ by
$F_i\mapsto f_i$, respectively $E_i\mapsto e_i$.

(b) **Positive quotient.** The quotient
$(U_A\otimes_Ak)/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to
$U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$; in it $\bar H_i=\bar T_{i,0,1}$ is the
classical coroot generator, $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$, and the positive
toral quotient is $k[H_i:i\in I]$ with kernel exactly
$(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$.

(c) **Operator form.** On every $U_A$-stable label-graded lattice the quotient
action of (b) is automatic: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$, the $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ act by
the integer binomials $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$, and all classical
Cartan and Serre operator relations hold, without any unproved global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness.

(d) **Boundaries.** The unquotiented specialization $U_A\otimes_Ak$ is *not*
identified with $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$: it retains toral characters,
as the integral $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-representation with $E=F=0$, $K=-1$ shows.
Extra Cartan directions of a regular realization act diagonally on
label-graded modules; they are not fabricated as generators of the toral
integral form, and direct substitution $q=1$ into vanishing denominators
$q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is never performed anywhere in this comparison.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, let
$U_A$ be the integral form with toral part $U_A^0$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]) and let $k$ be a
characteristic-zero field regarded as an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$.
Write $H_i:=T_{i,0,1}$ and $\bar x$ for the image of $x$ in a specialization.

(a) **Algebra level.** The positive toral quotient
$U_A^0\otimes_Ak/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is the polynomial algebra
$k[H_i:i\in I]$, and in it $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$ for all
$c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$
([[lem-rational-local-quantum-halves-and-torus-specialize-at-q-one]](c)).
No residual $K_h$-ambiguity remains after this quotient — the ideal
$(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is exactly the kernel of the comparison with
$k[H_i]$ — but it is *not* claimed that $K_h=1$ in the unquotiented
specialization $U_A^0\otimes_Ak$.

(b) **Label-graded lattices.** Let $M$ be a $P$-graded type-one
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module with label grading $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let
$M_A=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}(M_A\cap M_\mu)$ be a $U_A$-stable $A$-submodule that
is graded in the *lattice's own* sense, i.e. it is the direct sum of its
intersections with the label spaces. Then, on $M_A\otimes_Ak$, the operators
induced by $E_i,F_i$ (and all of $U_A$) satisfy: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$ for
every $h\in P^{\vee}$; $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ acts on the image of $M_A\cap M_\mu$ by
the integer $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$; and
$[\bar E_i,\bar F_j]=\delta_{ij}\bar H_i$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar E_j]=a_{ij}\bar E_j$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar F_j]=-a_{ij}\bar F_j$, where $\bar H_i$ acts on the image of
$M_A\cap M_\mu$ by the integer $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

The grading hypothesis in (b) is a real hypothesis on the lattice: it is not
inferred from the mere fact that $M_A$ spans a weight module. All divisions
that occur are performed inside the DVR
$R=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}$ (units $[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$); no vanishing
denominator $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is substituted by $q=1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module over $\mathbb Q(q)$ for a finite symmetrizable
Cartan datum such that

(a) $M$ is a weight module with $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}M_\mu<\infty$ for every
$\mu\in P$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]);

(b) the weight set $\mathrm{wt}(M)$ is bounded above: it is contained in a
finite union $\bigcup_{j=1}^s(\lambda_j-Q_+)$;

(c) $M$ is integrable, i.e. $E_i$ and $F_i$ act locally nilpotently for every
$i$.

Then $M$ is isomorphic to an algebraic direct sum of simple integrable highest
weight modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in P^+$
([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]);
concretely, every nonzero submodule of $M$ contains a maximal vector $v$ whose
cyclic submodule $U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$ for some
$\lambda\in P^+$, and $M$ is the direct sum of the submodules generated by the
vectors of any maximal independent family of simple submodules. AC is used
exactly to select a maximal independent family of simple submodules
simultaneously; restricted to any module generated by one finite-dimensional
$U^{\ge0}$-submodule the decomposition is obtained by a finite induction and is
choice-free. The finite-cone modules use the explicit label grading, and the
regularization supplier is used when the original pairing is not separating
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]]).

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight and let
$\tilde L(\lambda)$ be the nonzero integrable quotient of the Verma module
$M(\lambda)$ of [[lem-quantum-highest-weight-serre-quotient-is-integrable]]
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), with
highest vector $v_\lambda$ and label grading
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]). Put
$R:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}\subset\mathbb Q(q)$.

(a) **Character.** Every nonzero graded quotient $V$ of $\tilde L(\lambda)$
whose highest line is nonzero is generated by its highest vector and has in
every label the same dimension as the classical simple integrable highest
weight module of the regularized minimal realization of the same Cartan datum
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]],
[[thm-kac-moody-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]); in particular the
character is independent of $V$. No global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and
no crystal or global basis is used.

(b) **Uniqueness.** Consequently $\tilde L(\lambda)$ is simple, hence is the
canonical simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$, and every integrable cyclic
highest weight module of highest weight $\lambda$ is a quotient of
$L(\lambda)$.

(c) **The $R$-lattice.** For a nonzero highest vector $v$ of $V$, the lattice
$V_R:=\sum_wR\,F_wv$, summed over all ordinary words $w$ in the negative
generators, is stable under every generator of the integral form $U_A$ of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], is finite free over $R$ on each
label weight, and is generated by $v$ under $U_A$ after extension to $R$; its $q=1$ fibre
$V_R/(q-1)V_R$ is the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the
regularized minimal realization. Here the Gaussian binomials
$\binom{m}{r}_i$ of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]
are $R$-valued at integer labels, and the divided-power denominators
$[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$ are $R$-units.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

For a balanced triple, the two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If the triple is balanced and $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

derivations.claim: **Unconditional base change.** By [F1] and [F2] the fibre $V_A(\lambda)\otimes_AS$ is free over $S$ with basis $G_\lambda(b)\otimes1$, for every unital $S$; the rank of each finite weight component over $S$ equals $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu$ when $S$ is nontrivial, and the fibre still spans the extended module. No flatness is needed because the basis itself tensors.

**The $q=1$ specialization.** Put $R=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}$. The $R$-span of $V_A(\lambda)$ is exactly the ordinary-word lattice $V_R$ of the local comparison in [F3]: every divided word becomes an ordinary word times a product of the $R$-unit inverses $[r]_i!^{-1}$, and ordinary words already belong to $V_A(\lambda)$. Hence a characteristic-zero field fibre is the scalar extension of $V_R/(q-1)V_R$, which [F3] identifies with the classical simple integrable highest module. [[thm-weyl-kac-character-formula]] gives its Weyl–Kac character; in finite type the formal sum and product are finite, giving the Weyl character.

**Chart lattices.** The two chart lattices are read off from the $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-forms of the same free $\mathbb Z$-basis in [F4] and then localized at $0$ and $\infty$; since $q$ is a unit of $A$, there is no ring map $A\to A_0$ sending $q$ to $0$, so the charts are genuinely distinct from the base changes of step 1.1 and no specialization to $0$ is asserted.

**The root-of-unity boundary.** At a field specialization $q=\zeta$ with $\zeta$ invertible, [F5] vanishes the geometric factorial as soon as the index reaches the order $l>1$ of $\zeta_i^2$; since the divided powers in the integral basis are normalized by these factorials, the naive ordinary-generator description of the specialization may then fail, while the free basis $G_\lambda(b)\otimes1$ of step 1.1 is unaffected. If instead $\zeta_i^2=1$ in characteristic zero, [F5] gives $r!$ and no vanishing occurs, so that particular root-of-unity obstruction is absent.

**Conclusion.** Step 1.1 gives the unconditional free-basis base change with preserved finite weight ranks; step 2.1 gives the classical $q=1$ module and character; step 2.2 separates the chart lattices from specializations; step 2.3 identifies the exact scalar root-of-unity boundary, asserting no simplicity or semisimplicity claim.
