Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation over $\mathbb Q(v)$, where $v$ is an indeterminate and $v_i=v^{d_i}$; the transport below sends $v_i$ to $q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral, so $m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$
for all $i$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with highest vector
$v_\lambda$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).
Put $s_i:=F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$.

(i) Every $s_i$ is a singular (highest weight) vector of weight
$\lambda-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$.

(ii) The graded submodule
$S:=\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)s_i=\sum_iU_q^-s_i$ is proper, and the quotient
$\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/S$ is nonzero, has finite-dimensional
label-weight spaces, and is integrable ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

(iii) Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of highest weight
$\lambda$ is a quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices
with $a_{ij}\ne0$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put
$m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ and $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ for its displayed Serre
sums. Define $\omega,\psi,\tau:T\to T$ on generators by

$$\omega(E_i)=-F_i,\quad\omega(F_i)=-E_i,\quad\omega(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\psi(E_i)=E_i,\quad\psi(F_i)=F_i,\quad\psi(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\tau(E_i)=F_i,\quad\tau(F_i)=E_i,\quad\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}.$$

Here $\omega$ fixes $\mathbb Q(q)$, while $\psi$ and $\tau$ apply the field
involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ to coefficients; $\omega$ and $\psi$ extend as
algebra maps, and $\tau$ extends as an anti-algebra map. Each map preserves
$I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and descends to $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. All three are
involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a
semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear algebra
anti-involution. On the Serre sums,

$$\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij},\qquad\psi(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij},\qquad\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}.$$

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $\Phi\subseteq E$ be a reduced crystallographic root system with positive
system $\Phi^{+}$, simple roots $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$ and Weyl
group $W$, with inversion sets $N(w)$ and lengths $\ell(w)=|N(w)|$
([[def-length-and-longest-element-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]). Then:
1. for every $w\in W$, the length $\ell(w)$ equals the minimum number of
   simple reflections occurring in an expression of $w$ as a product of simple
   reflections;
2. there is a unique longest element $w_0\in W$; it satisfies
   $w_0(\Phi^{+})=\Phi^{-}$ and $\ell(w_0)=|\Phi^{+}|$.

Use the actual periodic based $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ module and its finite cuts of [[lem-two-cyclotomic-shears-give-a-periodic-integrable-based-sl-two-chain]]. Thus $n_{2k}=8k+2$, $n_{2k+1}=8k+4$, $p=q+q^{-1}$, $h=q^2+q^{-2}$, and $M^{(J)}$ keeps constituents $0,\ldots,J$ and shears only at indices less than $J$. On $(M^{(J)})^{\otimes2}$ let $\Psi_J=\Theta(\psi\otimes\psi)$ be the actual rank-one tensor bar, and put $e^{(J)}=b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$. Every sum and vector here is algebraic.

For each $J\ge1$, there is a unique $\Psi_J$-fixed vector $g^{(J)}$ with seed coefficient $1$ and strictly increasing first-weight corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. For every odd $j=2k+1\le J$, its coefficient $F_j(q)$ at $b_{j,0}\otimes b_{j,n_j}$ is independent of $J$ and satisfies

$$F_{2k+1}(q)\equiv(-1)^k(2k+1)!(q^3-q)\pmod{q^4+1}.$$

In particular this coefficient is nonzero. Every cut $J\ge1$ therefore has a nonzero corrected coordinate with constituent index at least $J-1$. For $L\ge J$, retaining the raw coordinates with both indices at most $J$ sends $g^{(L)}$ exactly to $g^{(J)}$, including at the last retained constituent where its outgoing shear has been omitted. No choice assumption is used.

derivations.claim: **Divided coproducts.** If $yx=q_i^{2\epsilon}xy$ with $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$, induction on $r$ gives $(x+y)^r/[r]_i!=\sum_{a+b=r}q_i^{\epsilon ab}x^ay^b/([a]_i![b]_i!)$. Multiplication on the right by $x+y$ gives the recurrence $c_{r+1,a}=q_i^{2\epsilon(r-a+1)}c_{r,a-1}+c_{r,a}$ for the ordinary-power coefficients $c_{r,a}=q_i^{\epsilon a(r-a)}\binom{r}{a}_i$ when $0\le a\le r$, extended by zero outside that range; substitution reduces it to $[r+1]_i=q_i^{\epsilon(r+1-a)}[a]_i+q_i^{-\epsilon a}[r+1-a]_i$, which follows by expanding quantum integers. For $F_i$, take $x=F_i\otimes1$, $y=K_i\otimes F_i$, $\epsilon=-1$ and $a=r-t$; for $E_i$, take $x=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}$, $y=1\otimes E_i$, $\epsilon=1$ and $a=t$. This proves the two formulas in [F1], including $r=0$ and both endpoint terms. Toral factors act on homogeneous vectors by Laurent units, so these coproducts preserve the relevant integral tensor lattices.

**Highest-first integral action.** Let $m=F_i^{(r)}m'$ be a homogeneous divided word of first height $h$, with $r\ge1$, and let $n\in N_A$. The base $v_\lambda\otimes n$ is preserved integrally by $\Psi$, since all positive components kill $v_\lambda$. For $t\ge1$ put $z_t=F_i^{(r-t)}m'\otimes F_i^{(t)}n$ and $a_t=q_i^{t(\mu(h_i)-r+t)}\in A$, where $m'$ has weight $\mu$. Formula [F1] gives $\Delta(F_i^{(r)})(m'\otimes n)=m\otimes n+\sum_{t=1}^ra_tz_t$. Semilinearity and bar compatibility give the exact recursion $\Psi(m\otimes n)=\Delta(F_i^{(r)})\Psi(m'\otimes n)-\sum_{t=1}^r\bar a_t\Psi(z_t)$. All tensors on the right have first height less than $h$, so induction makes their bars integral; the coproduct preserves the integral tensor lattice by [F1]. Divided words span $V_A(\lambda)$, hence $\Psi$ is integral on the whole tensor lattice. The factor bar is an integral bijection, so $\Theta$ is integral as well. The action is finite because first-factor raising is bounded by its highest cone.

**Lowest-second action (b).** Let $n=E_i^{(r)}n'$ be a homogeneous divided word in the lowest module, with $r\ge1$, and let $m\in M_A$ be homogeneous. If $n'$ has weight $\mu$, put $z_t=E_i^{(t)}m\otimes E_i^{(r-t)}n'$ and $a_t=q_i^{-t(\mu(h_i)+r-t)}$ for $t\ge1$. Indeed $K_i^{-t}$ in [F1] acts on the second factor after $E_i^{(r-t)}$, with scalar $q_i^{-t(\mu(h_i)+2(r-t))}$, which combines with $q_i^{t(r-t)}$ to give $a_t$. Thus $\Delta(E_i^{(r)})(m\otimes n')=m\otimes n+\sum_{t=1}^ra_tz_t$ and $\Psi(m\otimes n)=\Delta(E_i^{(r)})\Psi(m\otimes n')-\sum_{t=1}^r\bar a_t\Psi(z_t)$. All bars on the right have smaller second divided-word height. At height zero every positive-degree quasi-$R$ term kills the second lowest vector, so its bar is the integral factor bar. Induction and step 1.1 prove preservation of $M_A\otimes\omega V_A(\lambda)$; composing with the integral factor bar gives integral $\Theta$-action. The lower-cone support makes the action finite before evaluation. This proves (b).

**Finite-type action finiteness without multiplicity bounds.** First an integrable upper-cone module has reflection-stable label support: a nonzero admissible string position at label $\eta$ with top $\eta+n\alpha_i$ and top coroot $a=\langle\eta,h_iangle+2n$ has a nonzero mirrored position $a-n$ of label $\eta-\langle\eta,h_iangle\alpha_i$. Thus support is invariant under each $s_i$, and applying $w_0$ puts support in both $ igcup_j(\lambda_j-Q_+)$ and $ igcup_k(w_0\lambda_k+Q_+)$. Each upper/lower cone intersection has only finitely many labels: writing a label as $w_0\lambda_k+\gamma=\lambda_j- eta$ gives $ eta,\gamma\in Q_+$ with fixed sum $\lambda_j-w_0\lambda_k$, whose independent simple-root coordinates bound both terms. In particular the highest module of [F5] has finite label support and finite-dimensional label spaces, hence finite total dimension. Now let $m$ be any homogeneous vector of any integrable module, with no support or multiplicity restriction. Choose integers $a_i\ge0$ with $E_i^{a_i+1}m=0$. A sufficiently large dominant $\lambda\in Q\subseteq P$ exists even for a nonperfect datum: solve $Ax=\mathbf1$ over $\mathbb Q$, clear denominators and scale, so $\lambda=\sum_jx_j\alpha_j$ after this scaling has every $\langle\lambda,h_iangle$ a positive integer at least $a_i$. The map $U^+	o U^+m$, $u\mapsto um$, kills $\sum_iU^+E_i^{(\langle\lambda,h_iangle+1)}$, and by the half-exchange and highest presentation in [F5] its quotient is a copy of the finite-dimensional negative-half highest quotient as a vector space. Hence $U^+m$ is finite dimensional. Choose a finite homogeneous basis of this span; local nilpotence of every $F_i$ on its finitely many vectors gives common exponents. The same argument with the negative half shows that $U^-U^+m$ is finite dimensional. The torus preserves $U^+m$ because it is label graded, so triangular decomposition gives $Um=U^-U^0U^+m=U^-U^+m$. A general vector has finitely many homogeneous components and therefore also a finite-dimensional $U$-orbit. In particular $U^+m$ has only finitely many labels; if $U^+[
u]m
e0$, its label is $\operatorname{wt}(m)+
u$, so only finitely many $
u\in Q_+$ can act. This proves vectorwise finite quasi-$R$ action on arbitrary integrable finite-type modules. The divided coproducts in [F1] also prove tensor integrability: on a homogeneous pure tensor, every term of a sufficiently high simple-generator divided power has an exponent beyond the nilpotence bound of at least one factor, and toral factors only rescale homogeneous vectors. Finite maxima over finite sums and induction over the factors give integrability of finite tensor products, so the same argument proves finite successive quasi-$R$ actions there. It does not assert a finite raw-basis correction closure for arbitrary two-sided-unbounded based lattices.

**Finite-type universal coefficients (c).** In finite Cartan type choose a longest Weyl element $w_0$ and sufficiently large regular dominant weights as in [F4]. Building the lowest extremal vector by the reduced $w_0$-string of divided powers uses complete rank-one top-to-bottom strings, whose normalized norm factor at the end is $d_{a,a}=1$, and the extremal weight spaces are one-dimensional by the classical character comparison; hence the extremal vector is integral, bar fixed and of norm $1$, and by the norm-$1$ characterization it is the unique signed global element of its weight. The unsigned Chevalley map $\omega$ commutes with the normalized bar, so the normalized field isomorphism from the corresponding lowest module to the highest module is a form isometry and bar compatible, and its source integral lattice maps into the target because the extremal vector is integral and $U_A$-stable. Transported global vectors are integral, bar fixed, of residue norm $1$, hence are signed target global vectors; equal finite dimensions make this a signed integral lattice identification, sufficient for the coefficient test. Expanding $\Theta_
u$ in global half bases and applying it to the lowest extremal vector of a large highest module and the highest extremal vector of a large lowest module, the highest-first action of step 2.1 proves the output integral, and since distinct degrees have distinct weight pairs and the outputs are distinct actual $A$-basis vectors, every expansion coefficient lies in $A$. Hence $\Theta_
u\in U_A^+[
u]\otimes U_A^-[-
u]$, and the vectorwise finiteness proved in step 2.3 makes its action a finite sum on every arbitrary $U_A$-stable based pair. Each summand preserves the tensor lattice, so (c) follows without any weight-multiplicity restriction.

**The constructed highest and lowest classes (d).** Form right-associated products of highest modules. Highest-first action proves integrality of the normalized bar at every binary step, while the field cocycle of [F2] gives all parenthesizations the same bar without assuming integral action for intermediate arbitrary pairs. In the transfer order in which each positive-root component raises the first weight and lowers the second, only the degree-$0$ component fixes a label pair, so the bar is triangular with diagonal $1$. Every upward interval is finite by the upper-cone or finite-total-weight hypothesis, and for the lowest classes the lower-cone bound replaces finiteness of the whole mixed weight space. In a finite interval solve for a bar-fixed lift $g_t=e_t+\sum_{s>t}a_{ts}e_s$ with $a_{ts}\in q\mathbb Z[q]$, starting from the top: after subtracting the already constructed larger lifts, involutivity makes the remainder satisfy $f+\bar f=0$, whose unique positive $q$-part supplies the next correction. Finite induction gives existence, uniqueness and a unitriangular $A$-matrix with finite-interval inverse; the corrected family is an $A$-basis and an $A_0$-basis with the raw tensor crystal residues, is bar fixed, and has $A_\infty$-span the actual tensor bar chart.

**Closure under tensor constructions and based subquotients.** For a highest tensor object $P=V(\lambda_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes V(\lambda_m)$ and any based $N$, right-associate $P\otimes N$. Repeated highest-first action from step 2.1 makes every binary bar integral. The cocycle identifies this bar with the grouped one using the constructed bar of $P$, so $\Theta$ acts integrally on $P\otimes N$. The mirror argument uses step 2.2 for arbitrary first factor and a lowest tensor object. This includes pairs of constructed objects and proves the arbitrary-other-factor cases before inheritance. Based subobjects are spanned by subsets of the actual constructed bases and are therefore saturated, $(P_A\otimes Q_A)\cap(P'\otimes Q')=P'_A\otimes Q'_A$; $\Theta$ preserves their field submodules by its $U$-monomial terms, so integral action follows from the equality. Based quotient maps are $U$-linear, send basis to basis or $0$, have basis-subset kernel and commute with bars because both bars fix those bases; their integral tensor maps are surjective onto free complementary quotient lattices, so integral action descends. Direct sums are handled componentwise with the stated weight bounds. This proves closure of $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ and, dually, of $C_{\mathrm{low}}$, hence (d) for the pure classes, and for an ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix product each binary split has either a pure highest-class left block or a pure lowest-class right block, so one of the two action cases applies; every prefix transfer is bounded by a prefix upper cone or a complementary lowest suffix lower cone, so all correction intervals are finite.

**The affine boundaries.** For $A_1^{(1)}$, with $a_{01}=a_{10}=-2$, the degree-$\delta$ Kashiwara Gram matrix in the basis $F_0F_1,F_1F_0$ is $\begin{pmatrix}1&q^2\\q^2&1\end{pmatrix}$, so the correct $D$-coevaluation carries the factor $(q-q^{-1})^2/(1-q^4)=q^{-2}(1-q^2)/(1+q^2)\notin A$: the universal algebra-coefficient claim fails in affine type. For the stronger arbitrary-pair failure take $\lambda=\Lambda_0$, $\mu=\lambda-\delta$, $p=[2]$, and the global element $g=F_1F_0v_\lambda$; then $E_0g=0$, $E_1g=pF_0v$, $F_0^{(r)}g=0$ for $r\ge2$ by the length-three divided Serre relation, and $F_1g=pF_1^{(2)}F_0v$, $F_1^{(r)}g=0$ for $r\ge2$ by its rank-one length-two string. The integral based-quotient presentation therefore gives a $U_A$-map $V_A(\mu)/p\to V_A(\lambda)/p$ sending the highest vector to $g\bmod p$. For each global $h_b$ its image has bar-fixed coefficients in $A/(p)=\mathbb Z[i]$, whose bar-fixed subring is $\mathbb Z$; let $T_b$ be its unique integer-coordinate lift in the $\lambda$-global basis and set $c_b=h_b+T_b/p$. The free module $M_A$ with basis $\mathcal B_\lambda\cup\{c_b\}$ inside $V_\lambda\oplus V_\mu$ is $U_A$-stable because $UT_b-T(Uh_b)$ is divisible by $p$, all basis vectors are homogeneous and bar fixed, and because $1/p=q/(1+q^2)\in qA_0$ its exact chart and residue data equal the standard direct-sum based module, so all four based axioms hold. On the tensor $c_{\mathrm{top}}\otimes h_\mu$ the $\Theta$-action has the term $c_{\mathrm{top}}\otimes h_\mu-\frac{1-q^2}{1+q^2}v_\lambda\otimes g_\mu$, whose coefficient is not in $A$ and lies on a distinct tensor basis vector (the simple-root terms vanish by the displayed relations and every higher first raising degree vanishes). Hence unrestricted arbitrary-based $O_{\mathrm{int}}$ action is false, and the ordered or constructed hypotheses of (a)–(d) are necessary.

**Finite-type action does not imply supported globalization.** In [F6] every algebraic normalized lift of the specified seed would have finite raw support and coefficients in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ away from its seed. Project such a bar-fixed lift to a cut $J$ greater than its maximal constituent index by two. The projection has the same normalization, and finite-cut uniqueness in [F6] identifies it with the cut lift. That lift has a nonzero coordinate at constituent index at least $J-1$, outside the putative finite support, a contradiction. Thus the unrestricted construction assertion fails even in rank one, although the evaluated quasi-$R$ action is finite and integral. For balancedness, any element $g$ of the natural integral zero/bar intersection has both $g$ and $\Psi g$ with polynomial raw coefficients. The finite difference $w=\Psi g-g$ is anti-invariant; at its least first weight strict triangularity gives $\bar s=-s$ for a polynomial coefficient $s$, forcing $s=0$ and therefore $w=0$. Consequently a balanced seed lift would be such a finite fixed lift and is impossible. The residue condition and the least-first-weight argument eliminate all polynomial corrections at or below the seed weight, so such a balanced lift has the triangular normalization just contradicted. Finite-dimensional based pairs remain fully covered: their entire raw tensor basis is a finite correction closure. More generally integral finite-column triangularity with finite raw-basis correction closure gives the same finite correction and inverse used in step 3.2. This leaves all supported constructions of step 4.1 intact.

**Conclusion.** Steps 2.1–2.2 prove the highest-first and lowest-second action with integral lattice preservation; step 2.3 proves arbitrary-multiplicity finite-type action finiteness; step 3.1 proves the finite-type algebra coefficients $\Theta_
u\in U_A^+[
u]\otimes U_A^-[-
u]$; steps 3.2–4.1 construct the corrected tensor global basis, prove its triangularity with diagonal $1$ and establish the bounded highest/lowest construction and closure classes in (d); step 5.1 records the exact affine failure of the unrestricted statements. step 5.2 refutes only the unrestricted supported-globalization inference from case (c). The only Choice use is [C1].

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

For a balanced triple, the two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If the triple is balanced and $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

Let $M_1,M_2$ be integrable chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight modules with crystal bases $(L_1,B_1)$, $(L_2,B_2)$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]), and let $M_1\otimes M_2$ be the integrable module of [[lem-tensor-products-of-integrable-weight-modules-are-integrable]].

Then $(L_1\otimes_{A_0}L_2,\,B_1\otimes B_2)$ is a crystal basis of $M_1\otimes M_2$, and its crystal is the tensor product crystal $B_1\otimes B_2$ of [[def-tensor-product-of-crystals]]: for all $b_1\in B_1$, $b_2\in B_2$ and $i\in I$,

$$\tilde f_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde f_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)>\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde f_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\le\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}\qquad \tilde e_i(b_1\otimes b_2)=\begin{cases}\tilde e_ib_1\otimes b_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)\ge\varepsilon_i(b_2),\\ b_1\otimes\tilde e_ib_2,&\varphi_i(b_1)<\varepsilon_i(b_2),\end{cases}$$

with value $0$ as soon as the selected factor maps to $0$. In particular $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ map $B_1\otimes B_2$ into $(B_1\otimes B_2)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $b,b'\in B_1\otimes B_2$ one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$, so the partial-inverse axiom holds. The equality case $\varphi_i(b_1)=\varepsilon_i(b_2)$ is resolved as in the definition: $\tilde f_i$ acts on the second factor and $\tilde e_i$ on the first.

No finite dimensionality, bounded support or uniform nilpotence is assumed, and no choice principle is used.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

Let $\Phi\subseteq E$ be a reduced crystallographic root system with positive
system $\Phi^{+}$, simple roots $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$ and Weyl
group $W$, with inversion sets $N(w)$ and lengths $\ell(w)=|N(w)|$
([[def-length-and-longest-element-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]). Then:
1. for every $w\in W$, the length $\ell(w)$ equals the minimum number of
   simple reflections occurring in an expression of $w$ as a product of simple
   reflections;
2. there is a unique longest element $w_0\in W$; it satisfies
   $w_0(\Phi^{+})=\Phi^{-}$ and $\ell(w_0)=|\Phi^{+}|$.

Use the actual periodic based $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ module and its finite cuts of [[lem-two-cyclotomic-shears-give-a-periodic-integrable-based-sl-two-chain]]. Thus $n_{2k}=8k+2$, $n_{2k+1}=8k+4$, $p=q+q^{-1}$, $h=q^2+q^{-2}$, and $M^{(J)}$ keeps constituents $0,\ldots,J$ and shears only at indices less than $J$. On $(M^{(J)})^{\otimes2}$ let $\Psi_J=\Theta(\psi\otimes\psi)$ be the actual rank-one tensor bar, and put $e^{(J)}=b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$. Every sum and vector here is algebraic.

For each $J\ge1$, there is a unique $\Psi_J$-fixed vector $g^{(J)}$ with seed coefficient $1$ and strictly increasing first-weight corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. For every odd $j=2k+1\le J$, its coefficient $F_j(q)$ at $b_{j,0}\otimes b_{j,n_j}$ is independent of $J$ and satisfies

$$F_{2k+1}(q)\equiv(-1)^k(2k+1)!(q^3-q)\pmod{q^4+1}.$$

In particular this coefficient is nonzero. Every cut $J\ge1$ therefore has a nonzero corrected coordinate with constituent index at least $J-1$. For $L\ge J$, retaining the raw coordinates with both indices at most $J$ sends $g^{(L)}$ exactly to $g^{(J)}$, including at the last retained constituent where its outgoing shear has been omitted. No choice assumption is used.

derivations.claim: **Actual support bounds and finite correction closure.** The $O_{\mathrm{int}}$ hypothesis includes finite upper-cone support: for each factor $M_j$, $\operatorname{supp}M_j\subseteq\bigcup_a(\lambda_{j,a}-Q_+)$. Fix a total label $\mu$ and a choice of these finitely many upper labels. A tensor label tuple satisfies $\mu_j=\lambda_{j,a_j}-\beta_j$, $\beta_j\in Q_+$ and $\sum_j\beta_j=\sum_j\lambda_{j,a_j}-\mu$. Independent simple-root coordinates bound every coordinate of every $\beta_j$, so there are finitely many tuples, regardless of multiplicities at their labels. Every strict root transfer increases a prefix label by a nonzero element of $Q_+$; hence a chain of transfers visits no tuple twice and has bounded length. Each evaluated bar column is a finite sum of raw basis vectors: the tuple bounds permit only finitely many root degrees, each degree has a finite algebra expansion, and vectors in a field basis have finite support. Starting from a finite set of raw seeds, recursively adjoin the raw support of their bar columns. This is a finitely branching tree with the bounded strict-transfer depth just proved, so its closure is finite. The correction and inverse unitriangular transition therefore take place in a finite raw-basis set, even if some label spaces have infinite multiplicity. In finite Cartan type there is also a global label bound for every upper-cone integrable factor. Indeed a nonzero vector at $\eta$ has a nonzero admissible $i$-string position $F_i^{(n)}v$ with top $\eta+n\alpha_i$ and top coroot $a=\langle\eta,h_i\rangle+2n$; its mirrored position $a-n$ is nonzero by [F5] and has label $s_i\eta$. Thus support is stable under every $s_i$, including on nonseparating chosen label gradings. Applying the longest element $w_0$ shows that the same support lies in $\bigcup_b(w_0\lambda_b+Q_+)$. The intersection of an upper cone $\lambda_a-Q_+$ and a lower cone $w_0\lambda_b+Q_+$ consists of labels $w_0\lambda_b+\gamma$ with $0\le\gamma\le\lambda_a-w_0\lambda_b$ coefficientwise in the simple-root basis, so is finite or empty. The finite union of these intersections bounds the entire support. No finite-dimensional-weight-space inference for arbitrary based integrable modules is used. These arguments apply to the stated bounded category; an unrestricted two-sided-unbounded based pair still needs a separate finite-action and supported-correction proof.

**The field tensor bar.** For the empty sequence take the tensor unit $\mathbf 1=\mathbb Q(q)1$ of weight zero, with $u\cdot1=\varepsilon(u)1$: the counit of the quantum-group structure underlying [F1] has $\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0$ and $\varepsilon(K_h)=1$. Its basis is $\{1\}$, its crystal operators vanish, and its bar is $\Psi_{\varnothing}(f(q)1)=f(q^{-1})1$. These generator actions show integrability and bar compatibility; the divided-power lattice is $A\,1$, stable because positive divided powers act by zero and each $K_h$ acts by one and each $T_{i,c,t}$ acts by the Gaussian scalar $\binom{c}{t}_i\in A$. Its zero and infinity charts are $A_01$ and $A_\infty1=\Psi_{\varnothing}(A_01)$. A Laurent polynomial regular at zero has no negative powers and one regular at infinity has no positive powers, so $A\cap A_0\cap A_\infty=\mathbb Z$ and $A\cap A_0=\mathbb Z[q]$. Thus the balanced map of [F3] is $\mathbb Z1\to\mathbb Z[q]1/q\mathbb Z[q]1$, an isomorphism, and its unique global lift is $1$, with no correction. Every positive-root component of $\Theta$ annihilates a tensor pair containing this unit, since its positive or negative quantum half acts trivially there, while $\Theta_0=1$ acts as the identity; hence adjoining a unit leaves the tensor bar unchanged under the canonical unit identifications. The empty case is therefore vectorwise finite, involutive, integral, balanced and independent of parenthesization. For arbitrary integrable finite-Cartan factors, the supplier's finite-action clause proves tensor integrability and successive vectorwise finite quasi-$R$ evaluation without support or multiplicity bounds; the same field-bar calculations below therefore apply to those factors as well. For a single factor use its given bar. Define the binary bar $\Psi_{M,N}=\Theta(\psi_M\otimes\psi_N)$ and, for a finite sequence, the iterated composition; on each $O_{\mathrm{int}}$ factor pair the action of $\Theta$ is vectorwise finite by the explicit label-tuple bound in step 1.1; for the separately admitted ordered lowest inputs, the supplied lower-cone bounds hold before evaluation. $\Psi$ is semilinear because $\psi$ sends $q$ to $q^{-1}$. Since $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta$ by [F1], applying the binary bar twice gives $\Theta\overline\Theta=\mathrm{id}$, so $\Psi^2=\mathrm{id}$; and $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$ gives $\Psi(u x)=\psi(u)\Psi(x)$ for every $u$ and every tensor $x$ on which the action is defined.

**Integral preservation and triangularity.** In all the integral action cases of the supplier, including arbitrary based finite-type pairs, $\Psi$ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice and is an $A$-bijection because $\Psi^2=\mathrm{id}$; every positive-root component of $\Theta$ raises the first label and lowers the second, and only the degree-$0$ component fixes a label pair, so the action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is triangular with diagonal $1$ in the weight-transfer order. Finite raw-basis correction closure additionally holds in the bounded category by step 1.1 and in the separately supported ordered cases of [F2]; it is not inferred from unrestricted finite-type action integrality.

**Independence of parenthesizations.** For three factors the two bracketings compute $((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}$ and $((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23}$ composed with the factor bars, and the field cocycle of [F1] makes them equal coefficientwise; since every rebracketing of a finite sequence is generated by binary reassociations, all parenthesizations give the same $\Psi$, with all sums finite in each total root degree. This is the field-level assertion and requires no integral action.

**The corrected tensor global vectors.** Within the finite raw-basis closure proved in step 1.1, or the separately supplied bounded ordered interval, apply the semilinear correction algorithm of [F2]: in each such finite transfer interval solve $g_t=e_t+\sum_{s>t}a_{ts}e_s$ with $a_{ts}\in q\mathbb Z[q]$ for the bar-fixed lift of the raw vector $e_t$. Involutivity forces the remainder to satisfy $f+\bar f=0$, whose unique positive $q$-part supplies the next coefficient; finite induction yields existence and uniqueness of the corrected family, which is an $A$-basis of the tensor lattice congruent to the raw basis modulo $q$, and an $A_0$-basis whose residues are precisely the raw tensor crystal basis supplied by [F4]. The raw vectors themselves are generally not bar fixed, which is why the correction is needed.

**The integral balanced tensor triple.** Since the corrected family is $\Psi$-fixed, its $A_\infty$-span is the actual infinity chart $\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})$ and its $A_0$-span is the original tensor zero chart; intersecting the Laurent coefficient rings in this common basis gives the $\mathbb Z$-span as the balanced intersection $L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}}\cap\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})\cap A$-lattice, so the integral globalization isomorphisms of [F3] identify the corrected family as the genuine tensor global basis and prove integral balancedness. This uses the crystal lattice only as the residue datum and does not assert that $\Psi$ preserves $A_0$ or that the bar chart equals $L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}}$.

**Based subquotients and scope.** Exact based subobjects are saturated basis subsets and based quotients have basis-subset kernels; both commute with bars and crystal operators, and the image of a corrected global vector is integral and bar fixed with one raw residue or $0$, so balanced uniqueness [F3] proves the basis-or-$0$ compatibility and the corrected bases descend to exact tensor subquotients and direct sums within the stated bounds. Outside the listed cases no integral action is claimed, and the affine counterexample of the supplier shows it can fail; no universal braiding or semi-infinite evaluation is asserted.

**The unrestricted finite-type globalization boundary.** The actual integral rank-one bar in [F6] is algebraic and involutive but has no finite normalized lift of its seed: projecting a putative finite lift to a cut $J$ beyond its support by two identifies it, by finite-cut uniqueness, with a cut lift having a nonzero coordinate of index at least $J-1$. For the natural integral balanced map, an element $g$ of the zero/bar intersection has both $g$ and $\Psi g$ with polynomial raw coordinates. The anti-invariant difference $\Psi g-g$ must vanish: at its least first weight its polynomial coefficient satisfies $\bar s=-s$, hence is zero. The prescribed residue and the least-first-weight argument eliminate every polynomial correction at or below the seed weight. Thus a balanced lift of the seed would have the finite triangular normalization just contradicted. The resulting failure concerns the unrestricted based extension; steps 3.2–5.1 retain the entire supported full-tensor construction and its inheritance.

**Conclusion.** Step 1.1 proves the bounded-category finite-support bridge; steps 2.1 and 3.1 prove the well-defined semilinear involutive field bar and its parenthesization independence; steps 2.2, 3.2 and 4.1 prove integral preservation, the triangular correction, the corrected global basis and the balanced tensor triple in the supported construction cases; step 5.1 proves subquotient inheritance, and step 6.1 refutes unrestricted finite-type globalization while retaining the finite integral bar action.

citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

For a balanced triple, the two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If the triple is balanced and $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $q$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$$A_0:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}=\Big\{\frac fg\ :\ f,g\in\mathbb Q[q],\ g(0)\neq0\Big\}\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$$
be the localisation of the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q[q]$ at the prime ideal $(q)$ ([[def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal]]). By [[ex-the-local-ring-of-polynomials-at-x]] with $F=\mathbb Q$, the ring $A_0$ is exactly the ring of rational functions regular at $q=0$, it is a local ring ([[def-local-ring]]) with unique maximal ideal $qA_0$, and evaluation at $0$ induces an isomorphism $A_0/qA_0\cong\mathbb Q$. Since $\mathbb Q[q]$ is a principal ideal domain ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-pid]]) with nonzero prime ideal $(q)$, the ring $A_0$ is a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal; by the discrete valuation ring characterisations it is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser $q/1$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]], [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), and in particular a principal ideal domain ([[cor-dvr-is-a-pid]], [[def-principal-ideal-domain]]), with field of fractions $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[cor-rational-function-field-as-a-fraction-field]]).

By [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]] a discrete valuation ring is the valuation ring $V_v=\{x:v(x)\ge0\}$ of a discrete valuation $v$ on its fraction field. The discrete valuation of $\mathbb Q(q)$ with $V_v=A_0$ and $v(q)=1$ is the **$q$-adic valuation**; write it $\operatorname{ord}_q$, so that
$$\operatorname{ord}_q:\mathbb Q(q)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z\cup\{\infty\},\qquad A_0=\{h\in\mathbb Q(q):\operatorname{ord}_q(h)\ge0\},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_q(q)=1 .$$
Equivalently, $\operatorname{ord}_q$ is the vanishing order at $q=0$. The units of $A_0$ are exactly the fractions $f/g$ with $f(0)\neq0$ and $g(0)\neq0$, and $qA_0$ is the maximal ideal, so $q$ is a uniformiser of $A_0$ ([[thm-localisation-at-a-prime-is-local]]).

This ring $A_0$ is the **crystal limiting ring** of the crystal development below, and it is different from the Laurent ring $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ of [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]: $q^{-1}\in A\setminus A_0$, while $(1+q)^{-1}\in A_0\setminus A$; neither ring contains the other, and both are subrings of $\mathbb Q(q)$. For every free $A_0$-module $L$ the canonical map
$$\mathbb Q\otimes_{A_0}L\longrightarrow L/qL,\qquad c\otimes\ell\mapsto c\,\ell+qL,$$
is an isomorphism, and for every $\lambda\in\mathbb Q(q)^\times$ one has $\lambda L/q\lambda L\cong L/qL$; passing from $L$ to $L/qL$ is the **crystal limit**. No freeness of any further module, no lattice and no choice principle is asserted here.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

derivations.claim: **Witness (1): the balanced intersection and the missing residue class.** Write $a:=v+w$ and $t:=v$, so $L'=A_0a\oplus qA_0t$ and $V_A=Av\oplus Aw=Aa\oplus At$, while $V=\mathbb Q(q)a\oplus\mathbb Q(q)t$; these identities follow from $w=a-t$ and $v=t$. An element $\alpha a+\beta t$ with $\alpha\in A_0$, $\beta\in qA_0$ lies in $V_A=Av\oplus Aw$ exactly when $\alpha\in A_0\cap A=\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\beta\in qA_0\cap A=qZ[q]$, so $V_A\cap L'=\mathbb Z[q]a\oplus q\mathbb Z[q]t$. Similarly $\psi(L')=A_\infty a\oplus q^{-1}A_\infty t$, and the triple intersection is $$E_{\mathbb Z}=V_A\cap L'\cap\psi(L')=\bigl(\mathbb Z[q]\cap\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\bigr)a\oplus\bigl(q\mathbb Z[q]\cap q^{-1}\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\bigr)t=\mathbb Z a,$$ by [L4]. The integral residue of the zero chart is $(V_A\cap L')/(V_A\cap qL')=\mathbb Z[q]a/q\mathbb Z[q]a\oplus q\mathbb Z[q]t/q^2\mathbb Z[q]t$, which contains the nonzero class $qt+qL'=qv+qL'$. The balanced map sends $\mathbb Za$ onto the classes of integer multiples of $a$ and therefore misses that class, so the triple is not balanced by [L1].

**Witness (2): the rank-three balanced intersection.** For the trivial module $L''=q^{-1}A_0v$, so $V_A\cap L''=q^{-1}Z[q]v$ by [L4], and $\psi(L'')=qA_\infty v$, so $V_A\cap\psi(L'')=qA_\infty v\cap Av$. An element of $V_A\cap L''$ is $q^{-1}fv$ with $f\in\mathbb Z[q]$, and it lies in $qA_\infty v$ exactly when $q^{-2}f\in A_\infty$, i.e. when $f=0$ or $\deg f\le2$; hence $$E_{\mathbb Z}=V_A\cap L''\cap\psi(L'')=\mathbb Zq^{-1}v\oplus\mathbb Zv\oplus\mathbb Zqv,$$ the three Laurent monomials being exactly the integer-coefficient combinations with exponents between $-1$ and $1$.

**Witness (1): the lattice defects.** The vector $a=v+w$ is fixed by $\psi$, since $\psi(v)=v$, $\psi(w)=w$ and $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$ only acts on coefficients, and it lies in $L'$ with residue class $a+qL'$. But $a$ is a sum of two weight vectors of different weights, so $L'$ is not weight decomposed, and $\tilde e a=v\notin L'$ because $v=\beta t$ would require $\beta=1\notin qA_0$; thus $L'$ fails the crystal-lattice axioms of [L2] and the bar-fixed vector alone provides no parametrization or uniqueness.

**Witness (2): the kernel and the two lifts.** Since $V_A\cap qL''=q(q^{-1}Z[q])v=\mathbb Z[q]v$, the canonical integral residue map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(V_A\cap L'')/(V_A\cap qL'')=q^{-1}\mathbb Z[q]v/\mathbb Z[q]v$ is $(a_{-1}q^{-1}+a_0+a_1q)v\mapsto a_{-1}[q^{-1}v]$, which is onto with kernel $\mathbb Zv\oplus\mathbb Zqv\ne0$. The elements $g_1=(q+q^{-1})v$ and $g_2=(q+q^{-1})v+v=(q+q^{-1}+1)v$ both lie in $E_{\mathbb Z}$, both are fixed by $\psi$ because $\psi(q+q^{-1})=q+q^{-1}$ and $\psi(v)=v$, and both have residue class $q^{-1}v+qL''$; they are distinct since $g_2-g_1=v\ne0$. Hence the same nonzero crystal residue has two distinct bar-fixed integral lifts, and bar invariance plus congruence does not give uniqueness without the balanced isomorphism.

**Witness (2) is a genuine crystal lattice.** In the trivial module all Kashiwara operators vanish and $L''=q^{-1}A_0v$ is a full free $A_0$-lattice concentrated in the zero weight, with residue generator $q^{-1}v+qL''$; by [L2] it is a crystal lattice, so the failure of uniqueness in step 2.2 is not attributable to an invalid lattice. The genuine Kashiwara triples of [L5] require and possess the actual integral balanced map, which the present lattices do not have; accordingly no claim of the globalization theorem is contradicted.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 exhibit the nonbalanced lattice $L'$ whose bar-fixed vector $v+w$ cannot be globalized onto the residue class $qv+qL'$; steps 2.1–3.1 exhibit a valid crystal lattice with two distinct bar-fixed integral lifts of one nonzero crystal residue. Both conclusions are established by explicit coefficient computations in the displayed modules.
