citations.quote:
Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), fix $i\in I$, and write $f_i^{(n)}=F_i^n/[n]_i!$ for the divided powers ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent on $U_q^-$, and the endomorphism
$$P_i:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^mq_i^{-m(m-1)/2}F_i^{(m)}e_i'^{\,m}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-)$$
is well defined (each sum is finite on each element) and is the projection onto $\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$ along $f_iU_q^-$. In particular $e_i'P_i=0$, $P_iF_i=0$, $P_i^2=P_i$, $P_iu=u$ for $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$, and
$$U_q^-=\operatorname{Ker}e_i'\oplus f_iU_q^-.$$

(ii) Every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique $i$-string decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i',\qquad u_n=0\ \text{for }n\gg0,$$
and the components are given by $u_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_ie_i'^{\,n}u$.

(iii) The **Kashiwara operators on the negative half**, defined on the string decomposition by
$$\tilde e_iu:=\sum_{n\ge1}f_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_iu:=\sum_{n\ge0}f_i^{(n+1)}u_n,$$
are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear endomorphisms of $U_q^-$ with $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\operatorname{id}_{U_q^-}$; $\tilde e_iu=0$ if and only if $u\in\operatorname{Ker}e_i'$; $\tilde f_i$ is injective and $\tilde f_i(1)=F_i$. Both operators preserve the root grading and shift its degree by $\mp\alpha_i$, that is $\tilde e_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu+\alpha_i]$ and $\tilde f_i(U_q^-[-\nu])\subseteq U_q^-[-\nu-\alpha_i]$.

No choice principle is used. Here $e_i'^{\,n}$ denotes the ordinary $n$-fold power of the derivation, not its divided power. The same projector and every string coefficient preserve the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), as proved by the integral skew-string supplier; this does not assert that lattice's freeness.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation over $\mathbb Q(v)$, where $v$ is an indeterminate and $v_i=v^{d_i}$; the transport below sends $v_i$ to $q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S$ generated by $\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

derivations.claim: **Rank one.** By [L1] the lower global vector of the $n$-th class is $F^{(n)}$, bar fixed and congruent to it; by [L2] its Kashiwara norm is $1/[n]_{q^2}!$ and its Lusztig norm is the color-factor multiple $\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q^{2r})^{-1}=(1-q^2)^{-n}/[n]_{q^2}!$. Since $F^n=[n]_q!F^{(n)}$ and $[n]_q!$ is not a unit of $A$ for $n\ge2$, the ordinary power differs by a nonunit, and the Drinfeld generator pairing value $1/(q-q^{-1})$ records the remaining scalar.

**The two mixed $A_2$ vectors are lifts.** By [L3] the classes $\tilde f_1\tilde f_2\mathbf 1$ and $\tilde f_2\tilde f_1\mathbf 1$ equal $F_1F_2$ and $F_2F_1$; both are integral (products of generators), bar fixed ($\psi$ fixes each $F_i$ and reverses no letters here since $\psi$ is an algebra automorphism fixing $F_i$), and congruent to their distinct crystal residues, so by [L4] they are exactly the lower global lifts with no correction.

**The Gram matrices.** The diagonal pairings are $1$ by the normalization of the half form; the cross pairing $\langle F_1F_2,F_2F_1\rangle$ is computed by the adjunction with $e_1'$, using $e_1'(F_2F_1)=qF_2$ from [L3], giving $q$. Hence the Kashiwara Gram matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\q&1\end{pmatrix}$ with determinant $1-q^2$, and the transported Lusztig Gram matrix is its color-factor multiple $(1-q^2)^{-2}$ times it.

**Upper duals and the last degree.** Inverting the field Gram matrix gives the two displayed upper dual vectors, which are not the lower basis vectors; the reciprocal color factor multiplies the Lusztig form-duals by $(1-q^2)^2$. In degree $2\alpha_1$ the only class is that of $F_1^{(2)}$, whose norm is the rank-one value of step 1.1.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–3.1 exhibit the exact normalizations in rank one and in degree $\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ of $A_2$, the absence of triangular corrections in that degree, and the explicitly non-unimodular inverse-Gram duals. All displayed matrices and scalars are finite computations, and no false Gram-unimodularity is asserted.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 2.2), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 4.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

derivations.claim: **The norms.** The recurrence of [L1] with base $d_{m,0}=1$ gives the diagonal values; iterating it produces the closed form $d_{m,n}=q^{n(m-n)}\binom{m}{n}_q$ of [L2], and orthogonality between distinct labels makes the Gram matrix diagonal.

**Common crystal lattice and residues.** Put $C_0=\bigoplus_n\mathbb Z[q]w_n$ and $C_0^\vee=\bigoplus_n\mathbb Z[q]w_n^{\mathrm{up}}$. Since every $d_{m,n}$ is a unit of $A_0$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$, the inclusion maps identify $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z[q]}C_0$ and $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z[q]}C_0^\vee$ with $L_0=\bigoplus_nA_0w_n=\bigoplus_nA_0w_n^{\mathrm{up}}$, and the residues of $w_n$ and $w_n^{\mathrm{up}}$ are the same crystal class $b_n$; the upper operators are the weighted adjoints whose $q=0$ reductions reproduce the same partial-inverse string, while exact adjunction carries the ratios $d_{m,n}/d_{m,n\pm1}$ given by the duality theorem and so the corresponding unweighted adjunction holds modulo $q$ and generally fails exactly over $\mathbb Q(q)$.

**Bars for $m=2$.** The ordinary bar fixes $w_1$ but sends its upper denominator to $1+q^{-2}$, so it moves $w_1^{\mathrm{up}}$; the adjoint bar $\psi^\vee$ is characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$ and, on the diagonal form, fixes each $w_n^{\mathrm{up}}$. This is exactly the distinction between lower-bar and adjoint-bar fixedness asserted by the duality theorem, and no lower/upper basis equality is implied.

**The two lattices for $m=2$.** Substituting $m=2$: $d_{2,0}=1$, $d_{2,1}=q\binom{2}{1}_q=q(q+q^{-1})=1+q^2$, $d_{2,2}=1$. Hence $M_A=\bigoplus Aw_n$ and $M_A^\vee=Aw_0\oplus A(1+q^2)^{-1}w_1\oplus Aw_2$, whose middle quotient $(1+q^2)^{-1}A/A\cong A/(1+q^2)$ is nonzero: the map $a/(1+q^2)+A\mapsto a+(1+q^2)A$ is an isomorphism; in particular $M_A^\vee$ properly contains $M_A$ and the inclusion is not an isomorphism. For $m=1$, $d_{1,0}=d_{1,1}=1$ and the two lattices coincide.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–2.1 compute the rank-one norms, compare the two genuine $A$-lattices, exhibit the common crystal lattice and residues with modulo-$q$ adjoint agreement and the stated exact weighted adjunction, and identify the correct bar. All calculations are finite and use no determinant-unit assumption.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

For a balanced triple, the two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If the triple is balanced and $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. $$M\cap L_0\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cap L_\infty\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,$$
and the infinity residue map $E\to(M\cap L_\infty)/(M\cap q^{-1}L_\infty)$ is also an isomorphism; moreover $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_0$ and $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_\infty$ under the maps induced by inclusions. (2) If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps into $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, generates $M$ over $A$, and maps injectively into both rational residues $L_0/qL_0$ and $L_\infty/q^{-1}L_\infty$, then $F\cong E\cong(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$.

(3) More generally, let $N\subset M$ be an $A$-submodule whose integral intersection $E_N=N\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ satisfies $N\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_N$. If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps to $M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)$, generates $M$ modulo $N$ over $A$, and maps injectively into $(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$ and $(L_\infty+\mathbb QN)/(q^{-1}L_\infty+\mathbb QN)$, then $M$ is balanced. The sequence
$$0\to(N\cap L_0)/(N\cap qL_0)\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)\to(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$$
is exact, and its last image is the image of $F$. If $F$ and $E_N$ are finite free $\mathbb Z$-modules, then so is $E_M=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, and $M$ is free over $A$.

These are the integral forms of Kashiwara's chart lemmas, in the notation of [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]]; their rational base extension gives the usual $A_0/A_\infty$ criterion, and no containment of charts or freeness of $M$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $q$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$$A_0:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}=\Big\{\frac fg\ :\ f,g\in\mathbb Q[q],\ g(0)\neq0\Big\}\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$$
be the localisation of the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q[q]$ at the prime ideal $(q)$ ([[def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal]]). By [[ex-the-local-ring-of-polynomials-at-x]] with $F=\mathbb Q$, the ring $A_0$ is exactly the ring of rational functions regular at $q=0$, it is a local ring ([[def-local-ring]]) with unique maximal ideal $qA_0$, and evaluation at $0$ induces an isomorphism $A_0/qA_0\cong\mathbb Q$. Since $\mathbb Q[q]$ is a principal ideal domain ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-pid]]) with nonzero prime ideal $(q)$, the ring $A_0$ is a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal; by the discrete valuation ring characterisations it is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser $q/1$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]], [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), and in particular a principal ideal domain ([[cor-dvr-is-a-pid]], [[def-principal-ideal-domain]]), with field of fractions $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[cor-rational-function-field-as-a-fraction-field]]).

By [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]] a discrete valuation ring is the valuation ring $V_v=\{x:v(x)\ge0\}$ of a discrete valuation $v$ on its fraction field. The discrete valuation of $\mathbb Q(q)$ with $V_v=A_0$ and $v(q)=1$ is the **$q$-adic valuation**; write it $\operatorname{ord}_q$, so that
$$\operatorname{ord}_q:\mathbb Q(q)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z\cup\{\infty\},\qquad A_0=\{h\in\mathbb Q(q):\operatorname{ord}_q(h)\ge0\},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_q(q)=1 .$$
Equivalently, $\operatorname{ord}_q$ is the vanishing order at $q=0$. The units of $A_0$ are exactly the fractions $f/g$ with $f(0)\neq0$ and $g(0)\neq0$, and $qA_0$ is the maximal ideal, so $q$ is a uniformiser of $A_0$ ([[thm-localisation-at-a-prime-is-local]]).

This ring $A_0$ is the **crystal limiting ring** of the crystal development below, and it is different from the Laurent ring $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ of [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]: $q^{-1}\in A\setminus A_0$, while $(1+q)^{-1}\in A_0\setminus A$; neither ring contains the other, and both are subrings of $\mathbb Q(q)$. For every free $A_0$-module $L$ the canonical map
$$\mathbb Q\otimes_{A_0}L\longrightarrow L/qL,\qquad c\otimes\ell\mapsto c\,\ell+qL,$$
is an isomorphism, and for every $\lambda\in\mathbb Q(q)^\times$ one has $\lambda L/q\lambda L\cong L/qL$; passing from $L$ to $L/qL$ is the **crystal limit**. No freeness of any further module, no lattice and no choice principle is asserted here.

For any finite sequence of based integrable modules in the finite-weight-space category $O_{\mathrm{int}}$, the field tensor bar $\Psi=\Theta(\text{composite factor bars})$, built from the normalized intertwiner $\Theta$ of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]], is well defined, semilinear, $U$- and bar-compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations; all root-height sums are vectorwise finite.

For arbitrary four-axiom based integrable factors in finite Cartan type, the same field assertion and integral lattice preservation hold without multiplicity or global weight bounds, by the finite-action and universal integral-coefficient clauses of [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]]. Their actual bar is weight-transfer triangular with diagonal $1$. Finite action and integrality do not imply finite supported normalized global lifts: the periodic rank-one construction of [[lem-periodic-cyclotomic-based-sl-two-tensor-corrections-escape-every-finite-cut]] refutes that additional unrestricted assertion and the natural integral balanced tensor triple.

The full based and globalization assertion holds for bounded $O_{\mathrm{int}}$ pairs with independently established integral action (in particular for finite Cartan type), and for the supported construction cases of the supplier: highest-first or first $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest or $C_{\mathrm{low}}$ second; finite highest products and exact based subquotients and weight-admissible direct sums of their tensor constructions; and ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix products with their explicit support bounds. This includes the full finite-dimensional tensor product, with every constituent, in finite Cartan type. For any further class, the globalization assertion requires independently proved integral action and finite raw-basis correction closure in the strict weight-transfer order.

In these supported cases the actual tensor global vectors are uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts of the raw tensor residue vectors, with corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$; the transition and its inverse have finite columns, the corrected vectors form an $A$-basis, and the integral tensor triple is balanced. The $q=0$ tensor crystal lattice is supplied separately by [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], and its actual infinity chart is $\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})$. Exact based integral bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness, within these supported constructions. Raw tensor lower vectors need not be bar fixed. The affine boundary of the integral-action supplier still disproves arbitrary based-pair integral action in general type. derivations.claim: **The module triple.** By [L1] and [L3], $V_A\cap L_0=\mathbb Z[q]v\oplus\mathbb Z[q]w$, whose quotient by $q(V_A\cap L_0)$ has $\mathbb Z$-basis the classes of $v$ and $w$; the same two vectors are exactly $E_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Zv\oplus\mathbb Zw$, so the canonical reduction map is an isomorphism and the triple is balanced; its inverse, the integral globalization map, sends the two crystal classes to $v$ and $w$, respectively. The rational extension has basis the two classes over $\mathbb Q$. The lower global basis is $v,w$, congruent to the crystal classes.

**The string image.** The field string image is $FV=\mathbb Q(q)w$; the integral image ideal is $FV\cap V_A=Aw$, whose balanced part is $Aw\cap L_0\cap L_\infty=\mathbb Zw$. The three spaces are genuinely different, as displayed.

Work in quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ over $K=\mathbb Q(q)$, with $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and the divided-power integral form $U_A$. For $j\ge0$ put $\ell_j=j+3$, $n_j=j(j+3)$ and $r_j=j+2=\ell_j-1$. Let $V(n_j)$ have divided basis $u_{j,k}=F^{(k)}u_{j,0}$, $0\le k\le n_j$, of weight $n_j-2k$. Let $d_j=\varphi(2\ell_j)/2$ and $p_j=q^{-d_j}\Phi_{2\ell_j}(q)$, where $\Phi_m$ is the monic cyclotomic polynomial. Define $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}V(n_j)$ and the $K$-linear operator

$$T_j u_{j,t\ell_j}=(-1)^{t(\ell_j-1)}u_{j+1,r_j+t\ell_j}\quad(0\le t\le j),$$

with $T_j=0$ on every other divided basis vector. Define $S=\sum_{j\ge0}T_j/p_j$, $C=1+S$, and $b_{j,k}=C u_{j,k}$.

Then $S^2=0$; $C$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$ have finite columns on the algebraic direct sum; and $B=\{b_{j,k}\}$ is a homogeneous $K$-basis. Its free $A$-span $M_A=C(\bigoplus_j V_A(n_j))$ is $U_A$-stable. The standard compatible bar fixes every $b_{j,k}$. The regular zero and infinity charts, and their crystal residues, are exactly those of the standard direct sum of divided strings. Thus $(M,B)$ satisfies all four based-module axioms with integrability in place of finite-dimensionality, and its integral triple is balanced. No infinite vector or completed direct sum enters this construction. No choice assumption is needed.

For every $a\in U_A$, the raw-coordinate action is the finite-column operator

$$C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS.$$

In particular, with $G_j=\binom{n_{j+1}}{r_j}_q\ne0$,

$$E^{(r_j)}b_{j,0}=\frac{G_j}{p_j}b_{j+1,0}-\frac{G_j}{p_jp_{j+1}}b_{j+2,r_{j+1}},$$

and both displayed coefficients belong to $A$. This is a module-construction assertion; it does not assert a failure of tensor globalization.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

derivations.claim: Take the actual based chain of [F1] and the singleton seed $\{b_{0,0}\}$. Each vector of its field direct sum belongs to finitely many finite strings, so its $U$-orbit is finite dimensional. In particular $b_{0,0}=u_{0,0}+u_{1,2}/p_0$ belongs to $V(0)\oplus V(4)$. The seed therefore has a finite field orbit, while the question asks for a submodule spanned by raw basis vectors.

For every $j\ge0$, write $G_j=\begin{bmatrix}n_{j+1}\\r_j\end{bmatrix}_q\ne0$. Since $b_{j,0}=u_{j,0}+u_{j+1,r_j}/p_j$, [F2] gives $E^{(r_j)}b_{j,0}=(G_j/p_j)u_{j+1,0}$. Furthermore $u_{j+1,0}=b_{j+1,0}-u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}/p_{j+1}$. The index $r_{j+1}=j+3$ is strictly between $0$ and $\ell_{j+2}=j+5$, so $T_{j+2}u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}=0$ and $u_{j+2,r_{j+1}}=b_{j+2,r_{j+1}}$. Thus the exact raw expansion is $E^{(r_j)}b_{j,0}=(G_j/p_j)b_{j+1,0}-(G_j/(p_jp_{j+1}))b_{j+2,r_{j+1}}$. The two displayed raw vectors are distinct, and the first coefficient is nonzero.

Let $W$ be any $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$ and containing $b_{0,0}$. If $b_{j,0}\in W$, its image under $E^{(r_j)}$ belongs to $W$ by $U$-stability, and the nonzero $b_{j+1,0}$ coordinate in step 1.2 forces $b_{j+1,0}\in W$ by [F3]. Starting from $j=0$, induction therefore gives $b_{j,0}\in W$ for every $j\ge0$. These are infinitely many distinct members of the field basis $B$, so $W$ is infinite dimensional.

Hence no finite-dimensional based subobject of $M$ contains the singleton seed $b_{0,0}$. The module satisfies all four actual based axioms and is integrable in finite Cartan type by [F1], so it refutes the stated universal finite-envelope assertion.

derivations.claim: **Cyclotomic denominators.** For $m=2\ell\ge6$, primitive $m$th roots occur in inverse pairs and none equals $1$ or $-1$. Thus $\Phi_m$ has even degree $2d$, integer coefficients, constant term $1$, and is reciprocal. Consequently $p=q^{-d}\Phi_m(q)$ belongs to $A$, is bar fixed, and is irreducible up to a unit in the unique-factorization ring $A$. Moreover $1/p=q^d/\Phi_m(q)$ is regular at zero with strictly positive valuation; bar invariance gives strictly positive valuation at infinity in the parameter $q^{-1}$. Different values of $\ell$ give nonassociate irreducibles. Finally $p$ divides $[\ell]_q$, since a primitive $2\ell$th root is a simple zero of $q^\ell-q^{-\ell}$ and not a zero of $q-q^{-1}$.

**The needed Gaussian congruences.** Put $z=q^2$ and reduce modulo $\Phi_{2\ell}(q)$, so $z$ is a primitive $\ell$th root and $q^\ell=-1$. The finite identity $\prod_{h=0}^{N-1}(1+z^hX)=\sum_{k=0}^N z^{k(k-1)/2}\binom{N}{k}_zX^k$, proved by multiplying one factor at a time, and the block identity $\prod_{h=0}^{\ell-1}(1+z^hX)=1-(-X)^\ell$ give the Gaussian digit rule: a coefficient with lower remainder exceeding upper remainder modulo $\ell$ vanishes; when the remainders agree, the remaining coefficient comes from the ordinary binomial expansion of the full blocks. Since $\binom{N}{k}_q=q^{-k(N-k)}\binom{N}{k}_{q^2}$, for $r=\ell-1$ this gives $\binom{r+k}{k}_q=0\bmod p$ unless $k=t\ell$, and gives $\binom{r+t\ell}{t\ell}_q=(-1)^{t(\ell-1)}\bmod p$. Indeed the lower remainder is nonzero exactly in the vanishing cases, while in the other cases the unsymmetrized coefficient is $1$ and the symmetrizing factor is $q^{-t\ell(\ell-1)}=(-1)^{t(\ell-1)}$. The argument takes place in the integral domain $A/(p)$ and proves divisibility in $A$, rather than merely pointwise numerical vanishing.

**Modular divided-power homomorphisms.** Fix $j$, write $\ell=\ell_j$, $n=j\ell$, $r=\ell-1$ and $m=n+2r=n_{j+1}$. In $V_A(m)/(p_j)$, the vector $v=u_{j+1,r}$ has weight $n$. For $1\le a\le r$, the coefficient of $E^{(a)}v$ is $\binom{m-r+a}{a}_q=\binom{(j+1)\ell-1+a}{a}_q$, whose upper remainder $a-1$ is smaller than the lower remainder $a$; hence it is zero by step 2.1. For $a>r$ the action is already zero. Also $F^{(k)}v=\binom{r+k}{k}_q u_{j+1,r+k}$ vanishes modulo $p_j$ whenever $k>n$: until $k=(j+1)\ell-1$ its remainder is nonzero, and for $k\ge(j+1)\ell$ the target position exceeds $m$. Therefore $u_{j,k}\mapsto F^{(k)}v$ defines a homomorphism of the complete divided strings modulo $p_j$. To check all generators, divided $F$ compatibility is the Gaussian product identity for $F^{(a)}F^{(k)}$; divided $E$ compatibility follows by reordering $E^{(a)}F^{(k)}$ and using the just-proved annihilation of all positive divided $E$ powers on the weight-$n$ vector $v$, leaving exactly $\binom{n-k+a}{a}_q F^{(k-a)}v$; the vanished positions $k>n$ respect the source endpoints. Every toral generator and toral quantum binomial has the same weight scalar on matched positions. Step 2.1 identifies this homomorphism with $T_j$ modulo $p_j$, so $(aT_j-T_ja)V_A(n_j)\subseteq p_j V_A(n_{j+1})$ for every $a\in U_A$.

**Exact vanishing of consecutive shears.** The nonzero target positions of $T_j$ are $k=r_j+t\ell_j=(t+1)\ell_j-1$, $0\le t\le j$. Reduced modulo $\ell_{j+1}=\ell_j+1$, their residues are $\ell_j-t-1$, ranging from $2$ to $\ell_j-1$. None is zero. Since $T_{j+1}$ is supported precisely on positions divisible by $\ell_{j+1}$, one has $T_{j+1}T_j=0$ exactly. Other products $T_iT_j$ vanish because their source and target summands do not match. On every vector only finitely many $T_j$ act, so $S$ is algebraic, $S^2=0$, and $C^{-1}=1-S$. The equality $n_{j+1}=n_j+2r_j$ also shows each $T_j$ preserves weights.

Step 3.1 makes every column of $[a,T_j]/p_j$ integral. The only potentially nonzero summands of $SaS$ are $T_{j+1}aT_j/(p_{j+1}p_j)$. The numerator is divisible by $p_j$, because it equals $T_{j+1}(aT_j-T_ja)$ using $T_{j+1}T_j=0$; it is divisible by $p_{j+1}$, because it also equals $(T_{j+1}a-aT_{j+1})T_j$. These are entrywise divisibilities of matrices in standard divided bases. The distinct irreducibles $p_j,p_{j+1}$ are coprime in the unique-factorization ring $A$, so their product divides every entry. Thus all cross terms are integral. For every input column there are at most two shear positions, so all sums remain finite. It follows that $C^{-1}aC$ preserves $L_A$, equivalently $aM_A\subseteq M_A$. This checks the full divided-power integral form, not just $E$ and $F$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. derivations.claim: **The two denominators and the weights.** One has $p=q^{-1}\Phi_4$ and $h=q^{-2}\Phi_8$, so [F2] makes them nonassociate prime elements of $A$. Both are bar fixed, and $1/p=q/(1+q^2)$ and $1/h=q^2/(1+q^4)$ belong to $qA_0$ and, by bar invariance, to $q^{-1}A_\infty$. The source highest weight $n_j$ is divisible by $\ell_j$, and $n_{j+1}=n_j+2r_j$ for both parities. Hence every displayed target has the same weight as its source and lies in the target string.

**All the modular Gaussian coefficients.** For $\ell\in\{2,4\}$ reduce modulo $q^{-\ell/2}\Phi_{2\ell}(q)$, which is the corresponding $p_j$. Then $z=q^2$ has order $\ell$ and $q^\ell=-1$. The generating identity $\prod_{a=0}^{N-1}(1+z^aX)=\sum_t z^{t(t-1)/2}\binom Nt_zX^t$ follows by multiplication and the Gaussian recurrence; each full block of length $\ell$ is $1-(-X)^\ell$. It follows that a Gaussian coefficient with lower remainder larger than upper remainder modulo $\ell$ vanishes. For $r=\ell-1$ and $t\ge0$, the coefficient $\binom{r+t}{t}_{q}$ vanishes unless $t=v\ell$; in that case its unsymmetrized Gaussian value is $1$ and its symmetrizing factor is $q^{-v\ell(\ell-1)}=(-1)^v$, since $\ell$ is even. This gives exactly the coefficients of $T_j$ modulo $p_j$. All reductions are in the integral domain $A/(p_j)$, so they are divisibilities in $A$.

**Full divided-power intertwining modulo each denominator.** Fix $j$, put $n=n_j=a\ell_j$, $r=\ell_j-1$ and $m=n+2r$, and take $v=u_{j+1,r}$ in $V_A(m)/(p_j)$. Its weight is $n$. For $1\le t\le r$, the coefficient of $E^{(t)}v$ is $\binom{(a+1)\ell_j-1+t}{t}_q$, with upper remainder $t-1$ and lower remainder $t$, so it vanishes by step 2.1; larger $t$ give zero by the endpoint. Also $F^{(t)}v$ vanishes for every $t>n$: until $t=(a+1)\ell_j-1$ its nonzero remainder forces vanishing by step 2.1, and larger $t$ exceed the target endpoint. The assignment $u_{j,t}\mapsto F^{(t)}v$ therefore intertwines all divided $F$ actions by Gaussian multiplication. Divided $E$ reordering, using the annihilation of all positive divided $E$ powers on the weight-$n$ vector $v$, gives exactly $\binom{n-t+s}{s}_q F^{(t-s)}v$ for $E^{(s)}F^{(t)}v$, including zero beyond the source endpoints. Toral elements act by matched weight scalars. Step 2.1 identifies this assignment with $T_j$ modulo $p_j$, proving $[a,T_j]V_A(n_j)\subseteq p_jV_A(n_{j+1})$ for every $a\in U_A$.

**Algebraic invertibility and integral cross terms.** Every $T_j$ is supported on even positions and has odd target positions. Thus $T_{j+1}T_j=0$ exactly, and all other twofold products vanish by their summand indices. Every column is finite, so $S^2=0$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$ on the algebraic direct sum. For $a\in U_A$, expansion gives $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$. The commutator summands are integral by step 3.1. The only cross terms are $T_{j+1}aT_j/(p_{j+1}p_j)$. Their numerators are divisible by $p_j$, using $T_{j+1}(aT_j-T_ja)$, and by $p_{j+1}$, using $(T_{j+1}a-aT_{j+1})T_j$. Adjacent denominators are the two distinct primes of step 1.1, so their product divides every matrix entry by [F2]. The conjugated operator therefore preserves the standard free integral span, proving stability of the $B$-span. No nonadjacent repeated denominator creates a cross term.

**The compatible basis and crystal charts.** The inverse in step 4.1 proves that $B$ is a field basis with free integral span; its homogeneity is step 1.1. The coefficients $(-1)^t/p_j$ are bar fixed, so the standard module bar fixes $B$ and remains compatible with the algebra action. The module is integrable because every vector occupies finitely many finite standard strings. By step 1.1, $C$ and its inverse preserve both regular charts and are the identity on both residues, so the charts and crystal vertices coincide with the standard direct-sum ones. Their Kashiwara operators are exactly the finite shifts in [F1]. Thus all four conditions of [F3] hold.

**Balancedness, finite versions and exact column agreement.** In the common basis $B$, the three coefficient rings are $A,A_0,A_\infty$; their simultaneous intersection is $\mathbb Z$ and $A\cap A_0=\mathbb Z[q]$, since a Laurent polynomial regular at both ends is constant. Coefficientwise reduction therefore gives the integral balanced isomorphism, with finite support throughout. Omitting shears at indices at least $J$ preserves every preceding argument and gives the stated finite version. A standard action $a$ preserves each constituent summand; $C$ can raise the constituent index by at most one and $C^{-1}$ by at most one. Thus the raw column of $C^{-1}aC$ at index $j$ has indices at most $j+2$ and uses only shears with index at most $j+1$, all present when $J\ge j+2$; its finite and infinite computations agree. Finally the signs at positions $0,2$ in the first string give exactly the two stated seed formulas and factor weights. Every vector, map and index is specified explicitly, so no choice is used.

Put $K=\mathbb Q(q)$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $p=q+q^{-1}$ and $h=q^2+q^{-2}$. For $k\ge0$ set

$$n_{2k}=8k+2,\qquad n_{2k+1}=8k+4,\qquad \ell_{2k}=2,\qquad\ell_{2k+1}=4,\qquad r_j=\ell_j-1,$$

and set $p_j=p$ for even $j$ and $p_j=h$ for odd $j$. Let $u_{j,a}=F^{(a)}u_{j,0}$, $0\le a\le n_j$, be the divided basis of the highest string $V(n_j)$, of weight $n_j-2a$. On the algebraic module $M=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}V(n_j)$ define

$$T_j u_{j,t\ell_j}=(-1)^t u_{j+1,r_j+t\ell_j}\quad(0\le t\le n_j/\ell_j),$$

and define $T_j$ to be zero on all other divided basis vectors. Put $S=\sum_jT_j/p_j$, $C=1+S$, and $b_{j,a}=C u_{j,a}$.

Then $S^2=0$ and $C^{-1}=1-S$; these are finite-column algebraic operators. The homogeneous basis $B=\{b_{j,a}\}$ has a free $U_A$-stable integral span, its standard compatible bar fixes $B$, and its regular zero and infinity charts and crystal residues are those of the standard direct sum of divided strings. Thus it is an actual four-axiom based integrable finite-Cartan-type module, with a balanced integral triple and no choice assumption.

For every $J\ge0$, the finite version $M^{(J)}=\bigoplus_{0\le j\le J}V(n_j)$, with shears only for $j<J$, has the same properties. For every $a\in U_A$ the raw-coordinate action is $C^{-1}aC=a+[a,S]-SaS$; its column at a raw basis vector of index $j$ is supported at summand indices at most $j+2$. That column agrees with the finite version whenever $J\ge j+2$.

The raw seed $b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$ in two copies has total weight zero and factor weights $2,-2$. Both factors are deformed: $b_{0,0}=u_{0,0}+u_{1,1}/p$ and $b_{0,2}=u_{0,2}-u_{1,3}/p$. This statement constructs the modules and finite versions; it does not assert infinite tensor correction supports.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:

(i) $\Theta^{-1}=\overline\Theta=(\psi\otimes\psi)(\Theta)$, the inverse being taken in the root-height convolution algebra of $\widehat C$ and not switching the positive and negative tensor order;

(ii) for every $\nu$ the exact threefold identities hold:
$$(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}(1\otimes K_{-\eta}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{12}(1\otimes K_\eta\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{13},$$
with subscripts denoting tensor positions and $\Theta_{\nu'}=0$ when $\nu'\notin Q_+$;

(iii) the two normalized tensor-bar compositions satisfy the field cocycle identity
$$((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23},$$
coefficientwise in the transported source completion and on every vector for which the iterated actions are finite;

(iv) the bar-coproduct counterpart needed for the cocycle is
$$(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta_\nu=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=\nu}(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}(1\otimes K_{-\gamma}\otimes1)(\Theta_\eta)_{12}.$$

Removing the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ permits arbitrary scalar multiples of the same linear intertwiner equation, so normalization is essential for uniqueness; no integrality of coefficients and no uncontrolled infinite evaluation is asserted.

derivations.claim: **Finite cuts and their correction.** In a finite cut every evaluated degree is bounded by the finite divided strings, and [F2] is a finite sum of integral divided actions. Thus $\Psi_J$ is an integral semilinear involution. Degree zero is the identity, while degree $r>0$ raises first weight by $2r$. Finite first-weight induction constructs the corrected seed: at the next weight its residual is anti-bar by involutivity, so [F3] supplies its unique positive-polynomial correction. There are only finitely many raw vectors and weights in the cut, hence this process terminates. If two normalized fixed lifts differed, the coefficients at the least first weight of their difference would be in $q\mathbb Z[q]$ and equal their own bars, hence zero. This proves existence and uniqueness without an infinite completion.

**Projection coherence, including the cutoff.** Let $P_J$ keep raw tensor coordinates with both constituent indices at most $J$ and map them to the corresponding cut raw basis. To calculate a raw bar column, expand by $C\otimes C$, apply [F2], and reexpress by $C^{-1}\otimes C^{-1}$. All nonidentity expansion and reexpression terms increase a constituent index, and the middle operator preserves both indices. A term using the omitted outgoing shear at index $J$ is outside the retained rectangle and cannot return. An input outside that rectangle likewise cannot return. The retained raw columns are consequently exactly the cut columns, giving $P_J\Psi_L=\Psi_JP_J$ for $L\ge J$ and also $P_J\Psi=\Psi_JP_J$ for the algebraic full module. Since $P_J$ preserves the seed, weights and polynomial correction coefficients, step 1.1 gives $P_Jg^{(L)}=g^{(J)}$. This proves endpoint independence at the actual deleted-last-shear boundary.

**Four states and three transfer bands.** Work at total weight zero, and use first position $a$ and second bottom-distance $d$. The seed has $(a,d)=(0,0)$. On $0\le a,d\le3$, even shears send offsets $0\mapsto1$ and $2\mapsto3$, odd shears send only $0\mapsto3$, and inverse shears have the same supports. Degree $r$ decreases both offsets by $r$. Thus all reached raw coordinates remain in this envelope and $r\le3$. At first weight $2+2t$, both factors satisfy $n_j/2-a=t+1$ or $n_l/2-d=t+1$. For $t=4k+s$, $s=0,1,2,3$, the two possibilities are respectively $((2k,0),(2k+1,1))$, $((2k+1,0),(2k+2,3))$, $((2k+2,2),(2k+3,3))$, and $((2k+2,1),(2k+3,2))$. Order their tensor pairs $LL,LH,HL,HH$. Let $B_{t,r}$ be the four-by-four raw coefficient matrix from layer $t$ to $t+r$, obtained by the three finite operations of step 2.1. Then $B_{t,0}=I$ and there are no bands beyond $r=3$. The coefficient family $f_0=(1,0,0,0)^T$, $f_t=\mathcal P(\sum_{r=1}^{\min(3,t)}B_{t-r,r}\bar f_{t-r})$ is well defined layer by layer: each partial sum is a finite algebraic vector, its least unsolved residual is anti-bar, and the integral full bar makes that residual Laurent. No infinite vector is asserted to belong to the module. The symmetry of the shear signs and the two Gaussian factors in [F2] preserves $f_t=(P,Q,-Q,R)^T$.

**The scalar passed between four-layer cycles.** At layer $4k+1$, standard constituent $2k+2$ first appears, at offsets $(3,3)$, with coefficient $c_k=-(P-2hQ-h^2R)/h^2$. This follows by expanding the four raw states: the lower constituent is odd, its first top shear has coefficient $1/h$, and its second bottom shear has coefficient $-1/h$. Earlier layers cannot enter constituent $2k+2$, because odd shears require offset zero and that first occurs at this layer. At this point a future residual with an old first constituent is impossible above its top weight; a mixed new/old constituent term has an old second bottom or an old first top, so its positive quasi-$R$ terms vanish. The only remaining future residual is therefore $c_k(\Psi v_{2k+2,3;2k+2,3}-v_{2k+2,3;2k+2,3})$. Its initial center coefficient is bar fixed, since no earlier standard coordinate in this diagonal constituent can contribute to its first weight. Consequently the next four-layer correction depends only on $c_k$. Positive-part extraction is linear over $\mathbb Q$ (and over $\mathbb Z$ on integral coefficients); no linearity over $\mathbb Q(q)$ is claimed. In the induction below only the integer scalar $a_k$ is taken outside it. At $k=0$, [F2] gives $f_1=(-q^5+q^3-2q,-q^3+q,q^3-q,q)^T$, so $P-2hQ-h^2R=-p(h+1)$.

**Explicit matrices and integral ghost residual.** Let $E_{21}$ be the two-by-two matrix with its only nonzero entry $1$ at $(2,1)$, and put $D_t=(I+\alpha_tE_{21})\otimes(I-\alpha_tE_{21})$, with $\alpha_t=1/p,1/h,-1/p,0$ according as $t\bmod4=0,1,2,3$. This is exactly $C\otimes C$ between the four raw and standard states of step 3.1. For a source factor state $(j,a)$ and a target state $(j,a-r)$, put $\gamma(j,a,r)=\binom{n_j-a+r}{r}_q$; put the entry zero if that same constituent target is absent. Define $T_{t,r}$ on tensor pairs by $A_r\gamma(j,a,r)\gamma(l,d,r)$ in the matching target pair and zero elsewhere. Then the completely specified four-by-four matrices are $B_{t,r}=D_{t+r}^{-1}T_{t,r}D_t$. This includes $B_{t,0}=I$. For the diagonal ghost in step 4.1 the new string has $n=8k+10$, and its three positive divided coefficients are $G_r=\binom{8k+7+r}{r}_q$, $r=1,2,3$. Each $G_r$ is divisible by $h$: the upper and lower remainders modulo $4$ are respectively $(0,1),(1,2),(2,3)$, so the Gaussian block argument proved in the construction gives zero modulo $h$. Likewise $p\mid G_1,G_3$ by their upper/lower remainders modulo $2$. Thus $h^2\mid G_r^2$ for all three degrees, and $p^2h^2\mid G_r^2$ for degrees $1,3$. Reexpressing the resulting standard offset $3-r$ uses no shear for $r=2$, and at most the two denominators $p$ for $r=1,3$. Hence the future residual of the normalized rational ghost $-p((2k-1)h-1)/h^2$ has raw Laurent integer coefficients. Subsequent raw integral corrections preserve this property, and involutivity makes every least residual anti-bar. Thus the positive-part recursion used next has genuine Laurent input for every integer $k\ge0$, despite its initial rational ghost.

**Uniform quotient extraction.** Put $U_1=(0,0,0,-p((2k-1)h-1)/h^2)^T$ at layer $4k+1$, and set $U_i=\mathcal P(\sum_{r=1}^{\min(3,i-1)}B_{4k+i-r,r}\bar U_{i-r})$ for $i=2,3,4,5$. In the matrix formula of step 5.1 replace $\binom{8k+N}{r}_q$ by $\prod_{j=1}^r(zq^{N-j+1}-z^{-1}q^{-N+j-1})/(q^j-q^{-j})$; thus $z=q^{8k}$, and crossing a four-layer period replaces $z$ by $q^8z$. Write $k=3m+c$, $c=0,1,2$, and $x=q^{24m}$. Each residual is a finite Laurent polynomial in $x$ with rational $q,m$ coefficients. Polynomial division at infinity and removal of its constant term defines a $\mathbb Q(m)$-linear operator on these rational coefficients; on their Laurent sum it is exactly $\mathcal P$. Write each nonzero-$x$-power coefficient, after cancelling powers of $q$, as $N/D$ with $D(0)\ne0$. For positive $x$-powers the numerator is a polynomial with zero valuation at least $18$, and every negative-power coefficient has infinity degree at most $-18$; the finite bounds and denominator products are calculated below. Accordingly $q^{24am}N/D$ has zero constant at zero for $a>0,m\ge0$, and for $a<0$ its infinity degree is negative for all $m\ge0$, so contributes no polynomial part. If $a>0$ and $D\mid(q^{24}-1)^3$, put $u=q^{24}-1$ and $\rho=\operatorname{rem}_D(N(1+am\,u+am(am-1)u^2/2))$. The binomial expansion of $(1+u)^{am}$ is exact modulo $D$, including $m=0$ and $am=1$, because $u^3=0$ there. Thus $\rho=\operatorname{rem}_D(q^{24am}N)$, and Euclidean division gives the exact positive part $q^{24am}N/D-\rho/D+\rho(0)/D(0)$: the quotient's constant is $-\rho(0)/D(0)$, since the dividend vanishes at zero. For $x$-power zero, ordinary numerator/denominator division followed by constant removal applies, even if the coefficient has a pole at zero. These arguments justify extraction term by term, with no specialization at a root and no missing small-$m$ case.

**The finite all-parameter identity.** The following quotient/remainder identities result from substitution in the explicit matrices of step 5.1 and the extraction rule of step 6.1. Let $H=(q-1)(q+1)$, $J=q^2+1$, $K=q^4+1$, and $L=(q^2-q+1)(q^2+q+1)$. For residual layers $i=2,3,4,5$ respectively, the common denominators after removing powers of $q$ divide $HJK^2$, $H^2J^2K^2$, $H^3J^2K^2L$, and $H^3J^3K^2L$; the least positive-$x$-power zero valuations are respectively $18+16c,21+16c,22+16c,27+16c$, and the greatest negative-$x$-power infinity degrees are their negatives. All factors $H,J,K,L$ divide $q^{24}-1$, with their distinct cyclotomic factors pairwise relatively prime, and the displayed exponents are at most three; hence each listed denominator divides $(q^{24}-1)^3$. To obtain these identities form $T_{t,r}$ from its matching pairs, multiply on the two sides by $D_{t+r}^{-1},D_t$, collect powers of $x$, and for each positive power replace its remainder by the three-term polynomial of step 6.1; collect again after each of the four layers. The scalar $U_{5,LL}-hU_{5,LH}+hU_{5,HL}-h^2U_{5,HH}$ then has the following coefficients of $ph,p$, with all other coefficients zero: for $c=0$, $(-(216m^3+216m^2+66m+6),36m^2+30m+6)$; for $c=1$, $(-(216m^3+432m^2+282m+60),36m^2+54m+20)$; for $c=2$, $(-(216m^3+648m^2+642m+210),36m^2+78m+42)$. These are finite rational-function identities, verified by the indicated polynomial divisions; the formulas above specify every input and operation. Substitution of $k=3m+c$ in the three output pairs gives exactly $-(2k+2)(2k+3)p((2k+1)h-1)$. Since the extraction bounds include $m=0$, this proves the cycle identity for every $k\ge0$.

**Factorial invariant and nonzero endpoint.** Apply step 7.1 to step 4.1, using only linearity under the integer multiplier $a_k$. Starting with $a_0=1$, the scalar multiplier satisfies $a_{k+1}=-(2k+2)(2k+3)a_k$, hence $a_k=(-1)^k(2k+1)!$ and $P-2hQ-h^2R=a_kp((2k-1)h-1)$ at every odd layer $4k+1$. Modulo $q^4+1$, $h=0$ and $-p=q^3-q$, so the first coordinate $P$ has remainder $a_k(q^3-q)$. Its divisor is monic and the displayed nonzero remainder has smaller degree. This proves nonvanishing of every odd endpoint in the coefficient family.

**Identification with all finite cuts and conclusion.** For any fixed $J$, raw coordinate projection of the layerwise family is a finite vector: only finitely many raw states have both indices at most $J$. Step 2.1 shows that each coefficient equation projects to its cut equation; the seed and positive-polynomial corrections project as well. Step 1.1 therefore identifies this vector with $g^{(J)}$. In particular all retained odd endpoints have the formula from step 8.1. The largest odd index at most $J$ is $J$ or $J-1$, giving the claimed escaping support in every cut. The finite projection comparison was proved with the omitted outgoing shear, so no full-formal/cut identification has been assumed. Every parameter, basis and finite calculation is specified, and no choice is used.

Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at $0$ and at infinity, and the integral affine chart coordinate rings are $\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in P^+$. Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$, well defined by the highest-module presentation: its negative-half kernel is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}$, preserved by $\psi$ because every $F_i$ is fixed ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. Hence the quotient involution is compatible with the algebra action and fixes $v_\lambda$. Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]); both are $\psi$-stable. Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$.

The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction on this page, whereas $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice $M_A$. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. The intersections $M_A\cap L$ and $M_A\cap L^-$ are respectively $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-modules, generally not $A$-modules. The balanced part $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module; its Laurent extension $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$ is the full integral module once globalization is proved.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

Use the actual periodic based $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ module and its finite cuts of [[lem-two-cyclotomic-shears-give-a-periodic-integrable-based-sl-two-chain]]. Thus $n_{2k}=8k+2$, $n_{2k+1}=8k+4$, $p=q+q^{-1}$, $h=q^2+q^{-2}$, and $M^{(J)}$ keeps constituents $0,\ldots,J$ and shears only at indices less than $J$. On $(M^{(J)})^{\otimes2}$ let $\Psi_J=\Theta(\psi\otimes\psi)$ be the actual rank-one tensor bar, and put $e^{(J)}=b_{0,0}\otimes b_{0,2}$. Every sum and vector here is algebraic.

For each $J\ge1$, there is a unique $\Psi_J$-fixed vector $g^{(J)}$ with seed coefficient $1$ and strictly increasing first-weight corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$. For every odd $j=2k+1\le J$, its coefficient $F_j(q)$ at $b_{j,0}\otimes b_{j,n_j}$ is independent of $J$ and satisfies

$$F_{2k+1}(q)\equiv(-1)^k(2k+1)!(q^3-q)\pmod{q^4+1}.$$

In particular this coefficient is nonzero. Every cut $J\ge1$ therefore has a nonzero corrected coordinate with constituent index at least $J-1$. For $L\ge J$, retaining the raw coordinates with both indices at most $J$ sends $g^{(L)}$ exactly to $g^{(J)}$, including at the last retained constituent where its outgoing shear has been omitted. No choice assumption is used.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], let $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu$ be the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]]. Then:
